The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of a VR-assisted audiovisual intervention on acute physiological stress responses and patient-reported post-treatment feelings in adults with dental anxiety undergoing restorative procedures. MDAS was used only to characterize eligibility at baseline; post-intervention subjective anxiety was not assessed.

brief_summary: Zelicapavir is a novel orally administered non-fusion replication inhibitor of RSV that is being developed for the treatment of patients with RSV infection. This phase 2b/3 study will evaluate the efficacy and safety of zelicapavir compared with placebo in adults with RSV who are at high risk for severe disease. High-risk participants include those who are either ≥75 years of age or ≥18 years of age with COPD and/or CHF. Participants will be non-hospitalized adults who have up to 72 hours of respiratory tract infection symptoms and test positive for RSV.
primary_outcomes: Time to complete resolution of all 13 RSV symptoms as assessed by the Respiratory Infection Intensity and Impact Questionnaire (RiiQ) symptom scale
title: A Study to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of Zelicapavir Compared With Placebo in Adults With RSV Who Are at High Risk for Severe Disease

brief_summary:
Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies (DEEs) with a genetic cause represent a complex group of neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by intellectual disability and drug-resistant epilepsy. Because targeted, disease-modifying precision therapies like gene replacement and antisense oligonucleotides are rapidly approaching clinical trials, establishing objective diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic biomarkers is an urgent priority. Promoted by the IRCCS Istituto Giannina Gaslini and coordinated by Prof. Pasquale Striano, the MOBi-DEE protocol aims to identify and integrate multi-omic biomarkers using routine clinical investigations.

The study is designed as a multicenter, international, observational, cross-sectional, case-control, non-interventistico, and non-profit project targeting an enrollment of approximately 200 participants up to 55 years of age, including patients with genetically confirmed DEE and control subjects.

The methodology relies on biological samples and instrumental tests already collected during standard clinical follow-ups, avoiding any additional invasive procedures purely for research. Blood, urine, and stool samples are collected for metabolomic profiling, extracellular vesicle analysis, and gut microbiota metagenomics. Cerebrospinal fluid is analyzed exclusively if obtained as excess residual material from necessary diagnostic or therapeutic lumbar punctures or ventricular drains. Additionally, resting-state electroencephalogram recordings are evaluated via quantitative analysis to profile brain electrical dynamics, while electronic clinical report forms capture demographic data, genetic diagnoses, seizure characteristics, neurological status, and gastrointestinal symptoms via standardized questionnaires like Rome IV.

This research is vital for patients, families, and healthcare providers because it helps overcome the barrier of rare, heterogeneous patient populations through biomarker discovery, ultimately aiding the design of robust clinical trials for breakthrough therapies. By depending primarily on routine clinical samples and non-invasive collection methods, the study minimizes any added physical burden or risk for patients and families. Furthermore, strict data protection protocols govern privacy, while multi-centre material transfer agreements and future peer-reviewed publications aim to accelerate international research and therapeutic development.
primary_outcomes: Neurophysiological profiling of DEE patients.
Metabolomic profiling of DEE patients compared to controls across different biofluids (plasma, urine, stool, cerebrospinal fluid)
Gut microbiota profiling of DEE patients compared to controls
Profiling of extracellular vesicles identified in the analyzed biofluids of participants
title: Multi-biomarkers in DEE

brief_summary:
Neuromuscular diseases can cause weakness of the respiratory muscles, leading to respiratory pump failure and respiratory insufficiency. Compensation for respiratory pump weakness and/or impaired cough is achieved using devices that apply pressure to increase airflow and ensure effective ventilation. This technique can cause pneumothorax (separation of the lung from the chest wall), which can have potentially serious consequences.

We aim to determine whether pneumothorax is a frequent complication in this population. The results of this study would help optimize treatment and ensure the most appropriate prescription of these therapies.
interventions: Cough assistance device and/or thoracic mobilization and/or mechanical ventilation
primary_outcomes: Incidence of pneumothorax diagnosis in patients with neuromuscular diseases overall and according to the type of neuromuscular disorder.
title: Incidence and Risk Factors of Pneumothorax in Patients With Neuromuscular Diseases

brief_summary:
The objective of the study is to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the TMChM tendon prosthesis in the treatment of patients with chronic flexor tendon injuries of the fingers, compared with a reference tendon prosthesis currently used in clinical practice.

To achieve this objective, finger flexor tendon function will be assessed before and after implantation of either the TMChM tendon prosthesis or the reference prosthesis in patients with chronic flexor tendon injuries of the fingers.

The study is designed to demonstrate that the investigational TMChM tendon prosthesis is non-inferior in terms of effectiveness and safety to the prosthesis currently used in clinical practice.

The study aims to answer the following questions:

* Does the use of the TMChM finger flexor tendon prosthesis result in non-inferior functional outcomes, as assessed by finger tendon function parameters, in patients with chronic flexor tendon injuries compared with the prosthesis currently used in clinical practice?
* Can the TMChM tendon prosthesis be safely implanted using the intended surgical technique? The investigational medical device is the TMChM temporary finger flexor tendon prosthesis. The prosthesis incorporates an attachment for the FDS-FDP loop, enabling functional activation of the prosthesis and maintaining tension in the flexor muscles. Additionally, it allows for shaping of the FDS-FDP connection.

The patented TMChM temporary finger flexor tendon prosthesis features an attachment located at the proximal end of its silicone core. The prosthesis attachment has a semicircular cross-section, while the core has rounded sides and a rounded distal end.

The TMChM prosthesis is intended for implantation during the first stage of surgical treatment of chronic flexor tendon injuries of the fingers.

Furthermore, the TMChM prosthesis contains barium sulfate as a radiopaque marker, allowing it to be visualized during X-ray examinations.
interventions: Two-Stage Flexor Tendon Reconstruction with Temporary Tendon Prosthesis Implantation
primary_outcomes: Recovery of finger flexor tendon function
title: A National, Randomized, Single-blind Study Evaluating the Safety and Efficacy of the TMChM Prosthesis in the Treatment of People With Chronic Flexor Tendon Fingers Injuries Compared to the Prosthesis Used in Clinical Practice

brief_summary:
Emergency department (ED) visits have grown tremendously in Taiwan over the past few years, reaching approximately 7 million visits in 2019. This growth in ED visits has led to unprecedented levels of ED crowding, resulting in delays in care and increased morbidity and mortality in the ED. One of the complications of ED crowding is unsafe ED discharge leading to return ED visits. About 5-10% of the patients return to the ED within 3 days of the initial ED visit. Return visits are not only burdensome but also costly. Some return ED visits are even potentially dangerous, such as intensive care unit (ICU) admission, receiving emergency surgery or cardiac catheterization, and in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) during the revisit to the ED. These "high-risk" return ED visits are important in that they may reflect suboptimal initial ED care. Early identification of these high-risk events and appropriate interventions are critical for clinicians and patients. The investigators previously estimated that about 0.1% of the ED visits would become these high-risk ED visits.

High-risk revisits are relatively rare events, which require a large sample size for investigation. To this end, the increasing use of electronic health records (EHR) has opened the door to research rare events using big data. With the gradual adoption of EHR in major sections of the NTUH (outpatient in 2006; inpatient in 2007; and emergency department \[ED\] in 2009), investigators are now able to conduct clinical research using a wealth of data components in the EHR. For example, from 2013 to 2022, there have been \>1 million ED visits to the NTUH. The large sample size also enables studies of rare but important events, such as serious adverse events in return ED visits.

In this proposal, the investigators aim to develop and validate a vital-sign trajectory model (GBTM) and a machine learning/artificial intelligence (ML/AI) based prediction model for the high-risk ED revisits. The investigators will develop and validate these predictive tools using the NTUH data from 2013 to 2022, totaling approximately 1 million ED visits. In phase 2 (prospective validation), the investigators will prospectively collect data, fine tune our model, and optimize the system structure. In phase 3 (intervention), the investigators will embed the model into our hospital information system (HIS) in real-time to identify high-risk patients on ED discharge. If a patient is classified as high-risk, the computer user interface will recommend re-evaluating the patient and observing. At the discretion of the treating physician, wearable smart wristbands will be distributed to borderline high-risk patients who are still sent home to augment vital signs monitoring for 7 days. A dedicated case manager will review the records daily and consult the treating physician if red flags occur. A telemedicine session will be initiated if needed. The detection and intervention components together form the response system, the Emergency Department High-risk Revisits Prevention System (ED-HIKRS). In the intervention phase, the investigators will enroll and randomize 10 attending physicians into the ED-HIKRS or the usual care arm for 5 months, with each of them treating 200 patients (patients clustered within physicians). The pragmatic trial will stop for 2 months as a wash-out period, and an interim analysis will be performed. The physicians will then cross over, and each of them will treat 200 patients for another 5 months. A total of 4,000 adult patients will be enrolled. The primary outcome is the rate of high-risk revisits (ICU admission, receiving emergency surgery, and IHCA within 7 days of ED discharge) or same outcomes within 24 hours of hospitalization through the ED revisit. The secondary outcomes include general ED revisit rates, revisit admission rates, and ED mortality during the revisit.

The proposed study is highly significant because it addresses high-risk ED revisits, an understudied yet increasingly important area. The two state-of-the-art models, if successful, can be readily implemented in the EHR system for real-time prediction. The intervention of ED-HIKRS, if successful, may possibly intercept unsafe ED discharges and prevent subsequent serious adverse events. Our long-term goal is to deploy our system in existing clinical workflows to assist clinicians. This model may be generalizable to other health care systems countrywide.
primary_outcomes: The primary outcome is the rate of high-risk revisits (ICU admission, receiving emergency surgery, and IHCA within 7 days of ED discharge) or same outcomes within 24 hours of revisit hospitalization
title: Development, Validation, and Clinical Trial of a Prediction Tool for High-Risk Emergency Department Revisits

brief_summary:
The purpose of this clinical trial is to compare two different nerve block techniques-the Pericapsular Nerve Group (PENG) block and the Lumbar Erector Spinae Plane Block (L-ESPB)-for managing pain after hip fracture surgery in elderly patients.

Hip fractures are common in older adults and often cause significant pain. Managing this pain effectively helps patients recover faster and move around sooner after surgery. Traditional pain relief options include nerve blocks and strong pain medications (opioids). However, opioids can cause unwanted side effects like nausea and drowsiness, while some traditional nerve blocks can weaken the leg muscles, making early walking difficult.

Nerve blocks inject a local anesthetic (numbing medication) around specific nerves or within muscle layers to temporarily block pain signals:

1. PENG Block: Targets the specific sensory nerves supplying the front of the hip joint while minimizing leg muscle weakness.
2. Lumbar ESPB: Injects numbing medication near the lower spine to block pain signals coming from the hip region.

Participants in this study will include adults aged 60 and older undergoing hip surgery for a femoral neck fracture under spinal anesthesia. Participants will be randomly assigned (like flipping a coin) to receive either the PENG block or the Lumbar ESPB before their surgery. Both blocks are performed under ultrasound guidance to ensure precise medication placement.

Researchers will compare:

* Pain levels at rest and during movement over the first 48 hours after surgery.
* The total amount of additional pain medication (opioids) required.
* Leg muscle (quadriceps) strength after surgery.
* Any side effects or complications, as well as the overall length of hospital stay.

The findings from this study will help doctors determine which nerve block provides better pain relief while preserving leg strength, aiding in safer and faster recovery for elderly patients after hip surgery.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Pain Score on Movement at 12 Hours
title: Lumbar Erector Spinae Plane Block Versus PENG Block for Hip Fracture Surgery

brief_summary:
The goal of this Phase III randomized controlled, open-label clinical trial is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of adding peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) with Lutetium-177 DOTATATE to standard-of-care chemotherapy (CAPTEM), compared with CAPTEM alone, in adults with unresectable or metastatic, WHO Grade 3 well-differentiated gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs) with a Ki-67 index of \>20% to \<55% and positive somatostatin receptor imaging.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Whether the addition of PRRT to CAPTEM improves 1-year progression-free survival (PFS) compared with CAPTEM alone.
* Whether the addition of PRRT to CAPTEM results in differences in \*\*disease control rate, overall survival, treatment-related toxicity, and quality of life\*\* compared with CAPTEM alone.

Researchers will compare Arm A (CAPTEM alone) with Arm B (PRRT plus CAPTEM) to evaluate differences in progression-free survival, disease control, overall survival, toxicity, and quality of life between the two treatment groups. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either treatment arm.

Participants will:

* Undergo screening and baseline assessments, including physical examination, blood investigations, cardiac assessment, and imaging with Ga-68 DOTA PET/CT and FDG PET/CT.
* Receive CAPTEM (capecitabine and temozolomide) as oral chemotherapy according to the study protocol.
* If assigned to Arm B, receive four sessions of Lutetium-177 DOTATATE PRRT, at intervals of approximately 6-8 weeks, in addition to CAPTEM.
* Undergo regular clinical assessments, laboratory investigations, imaging assessments, and monitoring for adverse events and treatment-related toxicity.
* Complete EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-GINET21 questionnaires to assess quality of life.
* Continue follow-up after treatment, including clinical and imaging assessments, until disease progression or death.
primary_outcomes: 1-Year Progression-Free Survival (PFS)
title: TRINITY TRIAL; Trial Of PRRT Plus CAPTEM Vs CAPTEM Alone In Well Differentiated GEP NETS

brief_summary:
Objective: This study aims to examine the impact of postpartum home visits conducted by midwives or nurses within the framework of national health policies on the level of perceived social support and the quality of recovery among women in the postpartum period.

Methods: This research was conducted as an experimental study with a randomized, controlled, two-group, pre-test/post-test design. The study took place between February and June 2026, across 144 Family Medicine Units affiliated with 30 Family Health Centers in the Bağlar district of Diyarbakır. A total of 120 primiparous women in the postpartum period were included in the study; participants were randomized into intervention and control groups, stratified by family structure (nuclear versus extended family). Baseline assessments were performed during the initial postpartum primary care follow-up, and final assessments were completed on the 42nd postpartum day. In addition to standard postpartum care, the intervention group received three planned home visits from a midwife (the researcher), while the control group received standard postpartum care. Outcomes were evaluated using the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support (MSPSS) and the Quality of Postpartum Recovery Scale (QPRS).
interventions: Postpartum Home Visit-Based Midwife Support Program
primary_outcomes: Perceived Social Support
title: The Effect of Home Visits in Postnatal Care on Perceived Social Support and Quality of Recovery

brief_summary: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains a major global public health challenge. Despite continuous advancements in resuscitation strategies, overall survival rates remain low. High-quality chest compressions are the cornerstone of cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and current guidelines recommend compressions over the lower half of the sternum. However, accumulating evidence suggests that compressions at this location may result in aortic valve compression in approximately half of patients, impairing valve opening and obstructing forward blood flow from the heart, thereby diminishing resuscitation effectiveness. Both animal and human studies have consistently demonstrated a significant inverse association between aortic valve compression and survival outcomes. Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) enables real-time visualization of cardiac structures during ongoing chest compressions and can guide adjustment of the compression site to avoid aortic valve compression. The study team previously conducted an in-hospital randomized clinical trial of TEE-guided CPR (EXECT-CPR-1). Although improvements in physiologic indicators were observed, no statistically significant improvement in clinical outcomes was demonstrated. These findings support further investigation of whether earlier initiation of TEE-guided CPR in the prehospital setting can improve clinical outcomes. To evaluate this hypothesis, the present randomized clinical trial (EXECT-CPR-2) will leverage the nation's first prehospital physician rapid response system, in which physician-led teams are directly dispatched by the dispatch center to the scene of cardiac arrest. This approach aims to shift the initiation of TEE-guided intervention from the in-hospital to the prehospital phase. The study hypothesis, structured using the P-I-C-O framework, is that among patients with OHCA (P), those who receive prehospital TEE-guided chest compressions designed to avoid aortic valve compression (I), compared with conventional chest compressions over the lower half of the sternum (C), will achieve higher rates of return of spontaneous circulation (O), survival, and favorable neurological outcomes. A total of 204 patients will be enrolled over an estimated three-year period. This trial is expected to provide critical evidence to advance precision resuscitation medicine.
primary_outcomes: Any Return of Spontaneous Circulation
title: Execution of Prehospital Transesophageal Echocardiography During Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation in Patients With Out-of-hospital Cardiac Arrest

brief_summary:
Tobacco smoking is significantly more common among individuals with mood disorders, such as major depressive disorder (MDD) and bipolar disorder, compared to the general population. Chronic smoking in these conditions is often linked to more severe symptoms, frequent episodes, and reduced overall quality of life. However, the biological mechanisms linking tobacco smoking to brain alterations and clinical outcomes in mood disorders remain incompletely understood.

The primary purpose of this study is to examine whether chronic tobacco cigarette smoking is associated with alterations in brain structure, specifically regional brain volumes including the hippocampus and insula, and circulating biochemical markers of neuronal injury (neurofilament light chain \[NfL\]) and neurobiological pathways (tryptophan and kynurenic acid).

The study will enroll 240 male participants aged 18 to 45 years across six equal groups:

1. Major depressive disorder (in remission) who are current smokers
2. Major depressive disorder (in remission) who are lifetime never-smokers
3. Bipolar disorder who are current smokers
4. Bipolar disorder (in remission) who are lifetime never-smokers
5. Healthy controls who are current smokers
6. Healthy controls who are lifetime never-smokers

Participants will take part in a single study visit involving:

* Clinical assessments and psychiatric rating scales evaluating mood symptoms, cognition, personality traits, and smoking history.
* Routine physical and vital sign measurements.
* A fasting morning blood draw to evaluate serum biomarkers (NfL, tryptophan, kynurenic acid) and confirm tobacco exposure via serum cotinine.
* A structural brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan to measure regional brain volumes.
primary_outcomes: Normalized Hippocampal Volume
title: Neurostructural and Biochemical Signatures of Tobacco Smoking in Mood Disorders

brief_summary: Patients with suspected interstitial lung disease (ILD) may require a lung biopsy when clinical and imaging findings are inconclusive. This single-centre pilot study randomly assigns adults (1:1) to transbronchial lung cryobiopsy (TBLC) or to non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgical biopsy (NIVATS). Its main aims are to find out whether a larger trial is feasible (recruitment, acceptance of randomisation, completion of the assigned procedure, completeness of data) and to obtain preliminary estimates, with confidence intervals, of the diagnostic yield and the 30-day complication rate of each procedure. The study is not designed to demonstrate that one procedure is non-inferior or superior to the other; the results will be used to plan a multicentre confirmatory trial.
primary_outcomes: Histopathological diagnostic yield
title: TBLC vs NIVATS in Interstitial Lung Disease

brief_summary: Patients receiving inpatient treatment for substance use disorder may experience anxiety and depressive symptoms. Qigong is a mind-body exercise that combines gentle movements, breathing techniques, and relaxation. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of Qigong exercises on anxiety and depression levels. The study was conducted as a single-blind, randomized controlled trial. Patients meeting the predefined eligibility criteria were randomly assigned to either the intervention group or the control group. The intervention group participated in Shibashi Qigong exercises four times a week for three weeks (12 sessions in total), while the control group did not receive Qigong exercises. Both groups continued their usual treatments. Anxiety and depression levels were assessed using the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) and the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) at three time points: before the intervention, immediately after the three-week exercise program, and one week after its completion.
primary_outcomes: Change in Trait Anxiety Scores Measured by the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI-II)
Change in Depression Scores Measured by the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI)
title: Effects of Qigong Exercise on Anxiety and Depression in Patients Receiving Inpatient Treatment for Substance Use Disorder

brief_summary: The purpose of this research is to evaluate a brief digital single-session intervention designed to reduce internalized weight stigma among Dartmouth Health Weight Center patients. The study will examine whether the intervention is feasible, acceptable, safe, and helpful, and will examine how patients use and engage with the intervention in routine care. What we learn may help improve future approaches to reducing weight stigma and supporting patient well-being and engagement in care.
primary_outcomes: Weight Bias Internalization Scale - modified
title: Digital SSI to Reduce IWS

brief_summary: This is a prospective, single center, single-arm interventional study to evaluate the clinical utility of protocol-mandated diagnostic testing algorithm incorporating liquid biopsy and reflex tissue biopsy NGS for detection of ESR1 mutations in HR+/HER- metastatic breast cancer.
primary_outcomes: Number of participants with ESR1 mutations detected by reflex tissue NGS

brief_summary:
This single-site, prospective observational pilot study examines how clinically prescribed semaglutide is associated with changes in the adolescent brain, cognition, mood, interoception, and metabolic and biological markers. Adolescents 12 to 15 years old with obesity (body mass index at or above the 95th percentile for age and sex), whose own treating physician has independently decided to start weekly subcutaneous semaglutide (Wegovy) as part of routine care, complete multimodal assessments before starting the medication and again after approximately 6 months of treatment.

Assessments at each timepoint include 3T structural and resting-state functional MRI, a neurobehavioral and interoceptive battery, and saliva and blood collection for biomarker analysis and biobanking; a semi-structured qualitative interview is conducted at the follow-up visit. The study does not provide, prescribe, or modify the medication-all treatment decisions are made by the participant's own physician.

The primary goal is to characterize within-subject changes in resting-state functional connectivity, brain structure, cognition, and eating- and reward-related behavior associated with GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment during adolescence, and to interpret these measures relative to normative neuroimaging and cognitive data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study.
primary_outcomes: Change in resting-state functional connectivity in reward and default-mode networks
title: Brain and Obesity Longitudinal Development: Neurobiological Mechanisms of Semaglutide Treatment of Adolescent Obesity

brief_summary: The trial will assess the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of daraxonrasib monotherapy in Asian patients with RAS-mutated advanced biliary tract cancer in second-line treatment. The Primary Endpoint is Objective Response Rate (ORR).
primary_outcomes: Objective Response Rate (ORR)
title: Daraxonrasib in Asian RAS-mutant Biliary Tract Cancer

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a combined treatment of bevacizumab delivered directly to the brain tumour and a cannabis-based oral spray (nabiximols) can be given safely and practically alongside standard radiation and chemotherapy in adults with newly diagnosed glioblastoma. The main questions it aims to answer are:

How many participants have serious side effects (regimen-limiting toxicities) from the combined treatment? Can participants receive and complete the planned treatment, and how often does the catheter procedure succeed?

Participants will:

Receive standard care: radiation with the chemotherapy drug temozolomide Take a nabiximols (Sativex) mouth spray daily for 12 months, starting at 2 sprays a day and slowly increasing to the highest dose they tolerate (up to 12 sprays a day) Have three treatment sessions in which a thin catheter is guided through an artery to the tumour's blood vessels to deliver mannitol, which briefly opens the brain's protective barrier, followed by bevacizumab.
primary_outcomes: Regimen-Limiting Toxicity
title: Novel endOvascular Therapy With beVAcizumab and Cannabinoids for Glioblastoma

brief_summary:
HYPHOP is a multicenter, randomized clinical trial comparing two care pathways for women who need operative hysteroscopy to treat intrauterine lesions, such as uterine polyps, small submucosal fibroids, or retained pregnancy tissue.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. The first group will undergo hysteroscopic morcellation/aspiration in an outpatient consultation room, without requiring an operating room. The second group will undergo hysteroscopy using a resectoscope in the operating room, usually under general or regional anesthesia.

The main objective is to determine whether outpatient hysteroscopic morcellation/aspiration provides better value for money than conventional operating-room hysteroscopy, by comparing costs and health-related quality of life over six months from inclusion.

The study will also compare symptoms, quality of life, pain, complications, the need for further treatment, patient and practitioner satisfaction, and healthcare resource use. The hypothesis is that the outpatient care pathway may reduce costs without compromising patient outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Incremental cost-utility ratio of outpatient hysteroscopic morcellation/aspiration versus operating-room resectoscopy
title: Office Hysteroscopy Versus Operating-room Hysteroscopy for Uterine Lesions

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial was designed to evaluate the effects of topical black pepper (Piper nigrum L.) essential oil on vein visibility, palpability, and pain in children aged 7-12 years undergoing peripheral intravenous catheterization (PIVC) in a pediatric emergency department.

The study was conducted between March 2024 and March 2025 at the Pediatric Emergency Department of Istanbul University, Istanbul Faculty of Medicine, Türkiye. A total of 80 children were allocated to an intervention group (n=40) or a control group (n=40) using computer-generated simple randomization.

Children in the intervention group received 3 mL of a topical preparation containing 20% black pepper essential oil and 80% Aloe vera, applied to the planned catheterization site using a roll-on applicator. After a 10-minute waiting period, vein visibility and palpability were reassessed. Children in the control group received routine care without an additional topical intervention.

The primary outcome was vein visibility and palpability, assessed before the intervention and approximately 10 minutes later using the Vein Visibility and Palpability Score. The secondary outcome was pain intensity, assessed using the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) before catheterization and immediately after completion of the procedure.

Vein assessments were performed independently by two outcome assessors who were not informed of group allocation. The study aimed to investigate whether topical black pepper essential oil could improve vein prominence and reduce reported pain in children undergoing peripheral intravenous catheterization.
interventions: Topical Black Pepper Essential Oil Preparation
primary_outcomes: Change in Vein Visibility and Palpability
title: Effect of Topical Black Pepper Oil on Pain and Vein Visibility During Peripheral Intravenous Catheterization in Children

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate whether medial unloader bracing improves healing and clinical outcomes following arthroscopic medial meniscus posterior root repair. The primary aim is to compare 5-month MRI-based healing rates, meniscal extrusion, and cartilage changes between patients who use a medial unloader brace and those who do not following medial meniscus posterior root repair.
conditions: Arthroscopic Medial Meniscus Posterior Root Repair
primary_outcomes: Change in medial meniscal extrusion on coronal T2-weighted MRI at 5 months as defined by greater than 3 mm of extrusion from the tibial plateau.
title: Medial Unloader Brace After Root Repair

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of JZB32 in patients with vitreomacular traction (VMT). Based on a randomized, double-blind, multicenter, sham injection-controlled, parallel-group design, the proportion of study eyes achieving VMT resolution assessed by optical coherence tomography (OCT) at Day 28 will be compared between the JZB32 group and the sham injection group.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of study eyes with resolution of vitreomacular traction (VMT) assessed by OCT
title: A Phase II Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of Recombinant Human Truncated Plasmin Injection (JZB32) in Patients With Vitreomacular Traction

brief_summary: This trial is a 58 week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trial in which the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics of HB0056, either on top of stable IPF therapy or as monotherapy, are assessed in participants with IPF.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in FVC% (Percent of Predicted FVC value) to week 24
title: A Phase 2 Study of HB0056 in Patients With Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis

brief_summary: Blast injuries can cause swelling and pressure problems in more than one part of the body. This study will review existing medical records of people treated for blast-related injuries to learn how often these problems affect multiple body areas and whether they occur at the same time or one after another. Researchers will examine records for signs involving the abdomen, chest, limbs, or head, and explore how these findings relate to injury severity, resuscitation, organ function, and patient outcomes. No treatment will be assigned as part of this study, and patient care will not be changed.
lead_sponsor: Ukrainian Society of Regional Anesthesia and Pain Therapy
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Patients With Polycompartment Syndrome
title: From Blast Injury to Multicompartment Dysfunction:

brief_summary: This study will evaluate whether personalized digital oral-health education delivered through WhatsApp messages can improve oral hygiene in patients aged 16-25 years who wear fixed orthodontic appliances (braces). A total of 66 participants will be assigned to two groups. The intervention group will receive weekly digital oral-health messages for 12 weeks, while the control group will receive conventional verbal oral-hygiene instructions. Both groups will receive the same antibacterial mouthwash. Oral hygiene will be assessed at the beginning of the study and after 12 weeks by measuring plaque and gingival health using the Plaque Index and Gingival Index. The findings will help determine whether digital education can support conventional oral-hygiene instructions for patients undergoing orthodontic treatment.
conditions: Oral Hygiene in Patients With Fixed Orthodontic Appliances
interventions: Personalized Digital Oral Health Education via WhatsApp
lead_sponsor: Kurdistan Higher Council of Medical Specialties
primary_outcomes: Change in Plaque Index (PI) from Baseline to 12 Weeks
title: Effectiveness of Personalized Digital Oral Health Intervention in Patients With Fixed Orthodontic Appliances.

brief_summary:
Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is a three-dimensional spinal deformity that may be associated with misconceptions regarding its causes, symptoms, progression, and treatment. The Scoliosis Misconception Scale (SMS) was developed to assess patients' understanding and misconceptions about AIS.

This observational methodological study aims to cross-culturally adapt the SMS into Turkish and evaluate its psychometric properties in adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis. A total of 200 patients aged 10-17 years with AIS will be recruited. The Turkish version of the 17-item SMS will be administered, and test-retest reliability will be assessed in a subgroup of 50 participants approximately two weeks after the initial assessment.

The study will examine item-level measurement properties, internal consistency, and test-retest reliability. Item response theory analyses will also be considered, depending on model assumptions and sample adequacy. The findings are expected to provide evidence regarding the suitability of the Turkish SMS for assessing scoliosis-related misconceptions in Turkish-speaking adolescents.
primary_outcomes: Internal Consistency of the Turkish Scoliosis Misconception Scale
Test-Retest Reliability of the Turkish Scoliosis Misconception Scale
title: Turkish Adaptation and Validation of the Scoliosis Misconception Scale in Adolescents With Idiopathic Scoliosis

brief_summary:
The overall aim is to investigate whether genetic and other molecular markers can improve the diagnosis, assessment of treatment response, and detection of recurrence in patients with head and neck cancer. In the longer term, the project aims to contribute to more individualised treatment strategies for our patients.

The project will involve comprehensive analyses of tumour tissue and blood, including extensive genetic sequencing and other molecular profiling. Importantly, the research analyses will not have any implications for the clinical management or treatment of the individual patient included in the study.

Number of RNA alterations in head- and neck cancer based on RNA sequencing data

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to investigate the efficacy and safety of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor (sacubitril/valsartan) in preventing recurrence of atrial fibrillation after catheter ablation in non-hypertension patients with persistent atrial fibrillation.

This is a multicenter, randomized, open-label, parallel-group study in participants aged 18 to 79 years old who are hospitalized for planned catheter ablation of persistent atrial fibrillation and have a mean clinic blood pressure between 100/55 mmHg and 139/89 mmHg. The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does sacubitril/valsartan lower the proportion of late atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence after catheter ablation in non-hypertensive patients with persistent AF?
2. How safe is sacubitril/valsartan in people with persistent atrial fibrillation who do not have hypertension? Researchers will compare sacubitril/valsartan with standard care (routine post-ablation care without ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or ARNI) to see if sacubitril/valsartan prevents AF recurrence after ablation.

Participants will:

1. Be randomly assigned after ablation to receive sacubitril/valsartan or standard care.
2. Receive the assigned treatment and be followed for up to 12 months.
3. Attend clinic visits and tests to check for recurrent atrial arrhythmia and for safety.
4. Give blood samples before treatment and after 12 months of treatment for exploring potential molecular mechanisms.
primary_outcomes: The difference in the proportion of late atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence between the two treatment groups.
title: An Investigator-initiated, Prospective, Open-label, Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial, Comparing the Efficacy of Sacubitril/Valsartan and Standard Treatment on Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence After Catheter Ablation in Persistent Atrial Fibrillation Patients Without Hypertensive

brief_summary: Perioperative hypothermia (core temperature below 36.0 °C) is a common complication of surgery and is associated with increased blood loss, wound infection, cardiovascular events and patient discomfort. Forced-air warming (Bair Hugger) is the standard method of active warming. Resistive conductive warming (HotDog) transfers heat by direct contact and does not blow air into the operating room, which may be advantageous. This randomised trial will test whether resistive warming is not inferior to forced-air warming in preventing hypothermia on arrival in the post-anaesthesia care unit (PACU) in adults undergoing elective surgery under general anaesthesia.
lead_sponsor: Masarykova Nemocnice v Usti nad Labem, Krajska Zdravotni a.s.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of hypothermia on PACU arrival
title: Resistive Versus Forced-Air Warming for Prevention of Perioperative Hypothermia

brief_summary:
This study will compare three ways of giving radiotherapy to relieve symptoms caused by a large solid tumor. Radiotherapy uses radiation to treat cancer. Researchers want to find out whether LATTICE radiotherapy, which gives a higher dose to small areas inside a tumor while treating the rest with a lower dose, improves symptom relief compared with two treatments that give a more even dose.

The study plans to enroll 426 adults. One tumor must be at least 7 centimeters across and have a volume of at least 100 cubic centimeters. It must cause a symptom rated at least 4 on a 0-to-10 severity scale. The symptom may be pain, pressure or fullness, difficulty breathing or swallowing, bleeding, or difficulty with an activity because of the tumor. All three study treatments must be technically suitable for the person.

Participants will be assigned by chance, with an equal chance of receiving one of three treatments:

* A total dose of 20 gray over five treatment sessions, given evenly to the treatment area.
* A total dose of 25 gray over five sessions, given evenly to the treatment area.
* LATTICE radiotherapy: 20 gray over five sessions to the treatment area, with selected small regions inside the tumor receiving a total dose of 66.7 gray during those same sessions.

Gray is a unit of radiation dose. The 66.7-gray dose is the total dose to the selected regions, not an additional 66.7 gray on top of 20 gray. Each treatment is given once a day on five consecutive working days. Participants and their treatment teams will know which treatment has been assigned.

Before assignment, each participant will choose the single tumor-related symptom they most want treatment to improve. The main assessment is about eight weeks after treatment. A response requires a decrease of at least 2 points in this symptom score, while the participant remains alive and has not needed unplanned local treatment of the study tumor through day 63 after the final session. Death or this additional local treatment counts as nonresponse, even if symptoms improved earlier. A missing symptom score in a participant who is alive and has not needed this treatment is handled separately in the analysis.

Researchers will also assess how quickly symptom relief starts, how long it lasts, quality of life, side effects, tumor changes on scans, further treatment, hospital use and survival. Medical care needed for comfort or safety will not be withheld. Some questionnaires can be completed by telephone if a participant cannot or does not wish to attend; telephone calls do not replace required examinations, blood tests or scans.

Hospital stays and days alive outside hospital are assessed during the first 90 days after assignment, including people who do not start or finish radiotherapy. Side effects are recorded before treatment and during follow-up; the acute treatment-related assessment extends to 90 days after the last radiotherapy session actually received. The first 15 participants assigned to LATTICE will receive additional treatment-plan and safety review within the randomized study. Participants will be followed for at least 12 months, where survival permits, with record-based or direct follow-up extending to 24 months when possible. A planned review of missing outcome information, without examining treatment effects, may increase enrollment to a maximum of 480 participants.
interventions: Homogeneous External-Beam Radiotherapy, 20 Gy in Five Fractions
Homogeneous External-Beam Radiotherapy, 25 Gy in Five Fractions
LATTICE Radiotherapy, 20 Gy With a Simultaneous Integrated Boost to 66.7 Gy in Five Fractions
lead_sponsor: Affidea Nu-med Center of Oncological DIagnostics and Therapy
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants With Target-Symptom Response at Week 8
title: Comparing Radiotherapy Dose Strategies for Symptom Relief in Large Solid Tumors

brief_summary:
Smoking is a major public health concern associated with substantial morbidity and premature mortality. Planning may help people who wish to change their smoking behavior by translating their intentions into action.

Volitional help sheets (VHS) are brief, low-cost tools designed to support behavior change. They help individuals create personalized "if-then" plans by linking situations in which they may be tempted to smoke with strategies for responding to those situations.

Previous studies suggest that VHS may support changes in smoking and other health behaviors. However, they have mainly been evaluated in English-speaking populations, outside clinical settings, and as stand-alone interventions.

This pilot study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a smoking-specific volitional help sheet as an adjunct to care in a clinical setting.
primary_outcomes: Change in cigarette dependence as measured by the Cigarette Dependence Scale (CDS-12)
title: EFFECTIVENESS OF VOLITIONAL HELP SHEETS AS AN ADJUNCT TO TREATMENT TO PROMOTE BEHAVIOR CHANGE: A PILOT STUDY ON SMOKING

brief_summary:
Postoperative pain is a common concern following root canal retreatment. The type of root canal filling material and the technique used to place it may influence pain experienced after treatment.

This randomized clinical trial aims to compare the effects of two calcium silicate-based root canal filling materials (BioMTA+ and Well-Root PT) and two placement techniques (manual compaction and reverse-rotation compaction) on postoperative pain following nonsurgical endodontic retreatment.

A total of 56 adult patients requiring root canal retreatment due to persistent inflammation around the root tip will be randomly assigned to four treatment groups. All procedures will be performed in a single visit.

Postoperative pain will be evaluated using a visual analog scale (VAS), and the use of pain-relieving medication will be recorded.

The study aims to determine whether the type of filling material, the placement technique, or their combination influences postoperative pain following nonsurgical root canal retreatment.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Pain Intensity Assessed Using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
title: THE EFFECT OF FILLING MATERIAL AND PLACEMENT TECHNIQUE ON POSTOPERATIVE PAIN IN NON-SURGICAL ENDODONTIC RETREATMENT: A RANDOMIZED CLINICAL TRIAL

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if treatment with ticagrelor tablets can decrease inflammation in patients with Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD). Inflammation is thought to contribute to the risk of heart disease which is the leading cause of death in patients with CKD. Decreasing inflammation may decrease the risk of heart disease.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Why are patients with CKD at increased risk for heart disease and how to reduce that risk in the future.
* If there could be new treatment options for managing inflammation in blood of patients with CKD.

Researchers will compare Ticagrelor to a Placebo (a look-alike substance that contains no drug) to see if ticagrelor decreases inflammation in adult patients with CKD. A comparator (control) group not receiving the drug/placebo will consist of adults without CKD.

Participants with CKD will:

* Take ticagrelor 90 mg or placebo orally twice daily for 42 days
* Visit the clinic once every 2 weeks for checkups, tests, and bloodwork
* Participation will last approximately 12 weeks

Participants without CKD (control group) will visit the clinic twice (7 weeks apart) to provide information and bloodwork. Participation will last approximately 7 weeks with additional optional visits.
interventions: Ticagrelor: an oral, direct-acting, reversibly binding P2Y12 receptor antagonist
primary_outcomes: Aim 1: post-treatment IL-1β value
title: Ticagrelor for Inflammation and Cardiovascular Risk in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease

brief_summary:
Cervicogenic headache (CGH) is a secondary headache disorder originating from structural and functional impairments of the cervical spine, accounting for approximately 15-20% of all chronic headaches worldwide. It is characterized by unilateral head pain referred from the osseous, discal, or soft tissue elements of the upper cervical spine, frequently accompanied by restricted cervical range of motion, myofascial tenderness, significant neck disability, and disrupted sleep quality. Due to prolonged poor posture, repetitive neck movements, and increased sedentary lifestyles, the prevalence of cervicogenic headache has increased significantly in recent years. Although various physiotherapy interventions are available for its management, identifying the most effective conservative treatment approach remains a challenge due to the multifactorial nature and complexity of the condition, highlighting the need for further research. This study therefore aims to conduct the first randomized clinical trial directly comparing the effects of Dynamic Cupping and Facilitated Positional Release across five clinically relevant, multidimensional outcomes in patients with cervicogenic headache specifically pain intensity, headache impact, cervical range of motion, neck disability, and sleep quality.

The study design will be a randomized clinical trial. Non-probability Consecutive sampling technique will be used, and participants will be randomly allocated into two groups. Evaluation will be done using the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS), Headache Impact Test (HIT-6), Universal Goniometer (UG), Neck Disability Index (NDI), and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Group A will receive Dynamic Cupping therapy, while Group B will receive Facilitated Positional Release technique. Both groups will receive three treatment sessions per week over four weeks, totaling 12 sessions, alongside a standardized baseline conventional therapy comprising hot pack application and cervical muscle stretches and Isometrics. Measurements of all outcome variables will be taken at baseline and after 4 weeks. The collected data will be analyzed using SPSS version 25.
lead_sponsor: University of Management and Technology Lahore
primary_outcomes: Numeric Pain Rating Scale
Headache Impact Test-6 (HIT-6)
Universal Goniometer (UG)
Neck Disability Index (NDI)
Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI)
title: Comparative Effects of Dynamic Cupping and Facilitated Positional Release in Cervicogenic Headache

brief_summary:
This study aims to compare the effects of traditional resistance training and two different cluster set configurations on muscle strength, muscle hypertrophy, and explosive performance.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three resistance training groups: a traditional set group (TS), a cluster set group with three-repetition clusters (CS1), or a cluster set group with six-repetition clusters (CS2).

All groups will complete a six-week resistance training program involving half squats and bench presses. The training protocols will differ primarily in how repetitions and rest intervals are organized within and between sets.

Muscle strength, muscle size, and explosive performance will be assessed before and after the training intervention using standardized performance tests and body composition measurements.

The study aims to determine whether different distributions of rest periods during resistance training produce different adaptations in muscular strength, hypertrophy, and explosive performance.
primary_outcomes: Change in Half-Squat One-Repetition Maximum (1RM)
Change in Bench-Press One-Repetition Maximum (1RM)
Change in Pectoralis Major Cross-Sectional Area
Change in Bilateral Rectus Femoris Muscle Thickness
title: Effects of Traditional and Cluster Set Resistance Training on Muscle Strength, Hypertrophy, and Power

brief_summary:
This prospective cohort study aims to investigate the associations between the morphology of single-tooth implant-supported restorations, implant-related local factors, and peri-implant tissue health.

Participants receiving a single implant-supported restoration will undergo routine clinical follow-up. Peri-implant clinical parameters, supragingival and subgingival plaque, peri-implant crevicular fluid, intraoral scans, and periapical radiographs will be collected during routine follow-up visits.

The study will evaluate whether factors including implant three-dimensional position, restoration emergence profile, emergence angle, mucosal tunnel depth, restoration retention type, abutment type, and patient-related factors are associated with peri-implant inflammation, microbiological composition, marginal bone level, and peri-implant soft tissue changes.

The primary hypothesis is that deviation between the actual implant position and the digitally planned ideal implant position, as well as prosthetic emergence morphology, may be associated with peri-implant inflammation and changes in the local microbiome.
interventions: Because this is an observational study, no treatment is assigned by the investigators for research purposes.
lead_sponsor: Shanghai Ninth People's Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai Jiao Tong University
primary_outcomes: Peri-implant Bleeding on Probing
title: Association Between Peri-implant Tissue Health and Crown Shape: a Prospective Study

brief_summary:
The STREAMLINE-PVI trial is a prospective, single-center, randomized, open-label clinical trial comparing pulsed field ablation (PFA) with cryoballoon ablation (Cryo) for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF).

A total of 94 patients undergoing first-time PVI will be randomized 1:1 to either PFA or Cryo within standardized Lean Six Sigma (LSS)-optimized procedural workflows. The primary objective is to evaluate whether PFA reduces total procedure duration by at least 20% compared with Cryo without compromising safety or efficacy.

Secondary outcomes include post-procedural recovery, readiness for same-day discharge, atrial arrhythmia recurrence, AF burden, and procedural complications during a 12-month follow-up period.
primary_outcomes: Total Procedure Duration
title: Structured Treatment and Resource Efficiency Assessment With Lean Six Sigma Integration for Pulmonary Vein Isolation

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if targeted neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) can treat respiratory and peripheral muscle weakness in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does targeted NMES improve diaphragm thickening fraction and excursion as measured by diaphragm ultrasound?
* What are the comparative effects of targeted NMES on plasma biomarkers, specifically Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and Insulin-like Growth Factor-1 (IGF-1)? Researchers will compare three groups: the first intervention group receiving intercostal NMES combined with Pursed-Lip Breathing (PLB), the second intervention group receiving quadriceps NMES combined with PLB, and a control group receiving sham upper trapezius NMES combined with PLB, to see if targeted NMES provides superior improvements in respiratory and peripheral muscle function.

Participants will:

* Undergo baseline screening, including a diaphragm ultrasound and a blood draw for plasma biomarkers (IL-6 and IGF-1)
* Be randomly assigned to one of the three groups to receive either intercostal NMES, quadriceps NMES, or sham upper trapezius NMES, all combined with Pursed-Lip Breathing exercises
* Complete a post-intervention assessment involving repeat ultrasound imaging and biomarker analysis to evaluate muscle and systemic changes
primary_outcomes: Diaphragm Excursion (DE)
Diaphragm Thickening Fraction (TF)
title: Multimodal Assessment of NMES Effects on Respiratory and Peripheral Muscles in COPD

brief_summary: The aim of this study is to evaluate the activity status of two highly essential transcription factors (GR and PPARa), which are of crucial importance in the successful metabolic rearrangements (gluconeogenesis and fatty acid beta oxidation respectively) during sepsis, but which appear to lose their activity in a mouse model of septic peritonitis. Since these metabolic activities are located in liver, the activity status of these factors will be studied in livers of septic peritonitis patients and control patients, and will be related to metabolites in blood and to the disease status of these patients.
primary_outcomes: To study whether septic peritonitis patients have alterations in the expression levels of inflammatory genes linked to reduced activity of GR and PPARa in liver tissue.
To study whether human sepsis liver samples show an accumulation of FFA and alterations in collagen in liver.
To study whether there are indications for reduced activity of GR and PPARa in blood plasma.

To study whether there is a correlation between reduced GR/PPARa activity in the liver during sepsis and the general status of the septic patient (SOFA score), inflammatory markers such as IL6, TNF, procalcitonin, corticosterone or other metabolites.
To study whether septic peritonitis patients have alterations in the expression levels of metabolic genes linked to reduced activity of GR and PPARa in liver tissue.

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effects of tempo-controlled low-load resistance training compared to conventional low-load resistance training on pain, muscle performance, and functional disability in patients with knee osteoarthritis. The study will recruit 32 participants aged 40-65 with Grade I-II knee osteoarthritis and randomly allocate them into two groups for a 6-week intervention at Ch Rehmat Ali Memorial Trust Hospital. Group A will perform strengthening exercises (such as sit-to-stand, mini squats, and leg raises) using a controlled 3-1-3 second tempo cadence (eccentric, isometric hold, concentric), while Group B will perform the same exercises at a self-selected speed; both groups will receive preparatory moist heat, warm-ups, knee isometrics, and Maitland mobilizations three times weekly. Primary outcomes-including pain intensity (NPRS), functional difficulty (WOMAC), walking endurance (6MWT), and mobility (TUG)-will be evaluated at baseline and 6 weeks to determine if tempo control offers a more effective, well-tolerated alternative for managing knee osteoarthritis.
lead_sponsor: University of Management and Technology Lahore
primary_outcomes: Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS)
WOMAC Function Subscale
Six-Minute Walk Test (6MWT)
Timed Up and Go (TUG) Test
title: Tempo-controlled Low-load Resistance Training in Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis.

brief_summary: Mosquitoes spread diseases such as malaria, but tracking mosquito populations is often slow and depends on a small number of highly trained specialists. VectorCam is a smartphone-based tool that uses artificial intelligence (AI) to help identify mosquitoes from photographs and automatically report surveillance information. In this study, community health workers in Uganda used VectorCam during routine mosquito collection activities, while a comparison group followed standard methods that required mosquito identification by trained specialists using microscopes. The study evaluated how accurately mosquitoes could be identified, how quickly information could be reported, how complete the collected data were, and how easy the system was to use. The goal was to determine whether AI-enabled technology could help communities collect and share mosquito surveillance information more quickly and efficiently, while maintaining data quality under real-world conditions.
primary_outcomes: Mosquito Species Identification Accuracy
Throughput Efficiency (Per-specimen identification time )
Completeness (proportion of required surveillance reporting fields successfully captured and available)
Timeliness (delay between field specimen collection and availability of surveillance data)
title: VectorCAM: A Digital Innovation to Advance Entomological Surveillance

brief_summary:
Researchers are looking for new ways to treat limited-stage small cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC). LS-SCLC is a type of lung cancer that has not spread from the lung to other parts of the body. Researchers want to learn if gocatamig given with durvalumab can treat LS-SCLC.

The main goal of this trial is to learn if participants who receive gocatamig with durvalumab live longer without the cancer getting worse than those who receive durvalumab alone.
primary_outcomes: Progression-Free Survival (PFS)
title: A Clinical Trial of Gocatamig (MK-6070) With Durvalumab in Participants With Small Cell Lung Cancer (MK-6070-004)

brief_summary:
This study examines whether transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), a non-invasive form of brain stimulation, influences cyberaggressive behaviour in adults. tDCS uses a weak electrical current applied through electrodes placed on the scalp.

Participants will be randomly assigned to receive one of three types of stimulation: anodal, cathodal, or sham stimulation. They will attend three study sessions on three consecutive days and will receive the same assigned stimulation condition at each session. During the study, participants will complete computer-based tasks involving cognitive performance, social interaction, and responses to provocation.

The main purpose of the study is to determine whether cyberaggressive responding after the third stimulation session differs between the three stimulation conditions. Cyberaggressive behaviour will be assessed using a competitive online interaction task in which participants can respond to messages from another player. The study will also collect additional behavioural and physiological measures to better understand responses during the tasks.
primary_outcomes: Cyberaggressive responding on the TAP-Chat task
title: Effects of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation on Cyberaggressive Behaviour in Adults

brief_summary:
Cardiac rehabilitation is an important part of the treatment of patients with cardiovascular disease. Supervised aerobic exercise improves physical fitness, functional capacity, and quality of life. However, the most effective method for prescribing exercise intensity during cardiac rehabilitation remains uncertain.

The T-REXI-CR trial aims to determine whether prescribing aerobic exercise intensity based on individual ventilatory thresholds leads to greater improvements in functional capacity than the guideline-recommended approach based on heart rate reserve.

This pragmatic, multicentre, randomised controlled trial will compare two exercise intensity prescription strategies in patients participating in cardiac rehabilitation programmes in Belgium.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups:

* Threshold-based prescription: Exercise intensity will be individually prescribed using the first and second ventilatory thresholds (VT1 and VT2) identified during cardiopulmonary exercise testing.
* Range-based prescription: Exercise intensity will be prescribed using the guideline-recommended range of 40-69% of heart rate reserve.

Both groups will participate in a 15-week supervised aerobic exercise programme, targeting 40 exercise sessions. The programmes will follow the same training structure and progression principles, differing primarily in the method used to determine exercise intensity.

The study will assess whether threshold-based exercise prescription provides additional benefits compared with conventional range-based prescription, with the aim of informing clinical practice and improving the delivery of cardiac rehabilitation.
primary_outcomes: Change in Peak Oxygen Uptake (VO2peak) From Baseline to 4 Months
title: Threshold-Based Versus Range-Based Exercise Intensity Prescription in Cardiac Rehabilitation

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn about cognitive function and brain imaging findings in people with glycogen storage disease (GSD). The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do people with GSD perform differently on cognitive tests from people without GSD?
* Do brain volume, brain structure, intracranial blood vessels, and blood flow differ between the two groups, and are these findings related to cognitive test results or measures of metabolic control? Researchers will compare people with GSD with healthy volunteers of similar age and sex. No treatment will be assigned as part of the study.

Participants will:

* Complete cognitive tests
* Have a brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan using a 3-tesla scanner
* Provide relevant medical history and clinical information
primary_outcomes: Cognitive impairment
title: Neurocognitive Function and Neuroimaging Features in Patients With Glycogen Storage Diseases

brief_summary: The aim of this study is to assess the short-term outcomes of endoscopic extended totally extraperitoneal repair in primary small-sized ventral hernias, with specific regard to surgical site occurrences and hernia recurrence.
interventions: Group I:Extended Totally Extraperitoneal Retro-muscular Repair
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Morbidity (Surgical Field Occurrence/Surgical Site Occurrence)

brief_summary:
This study examined changes in environmental worry and related feelings among second-grade primary school children who participated in an Eco-STEAM educational programme in Istanbul, Turkey. Eco-STEAM combines ecology activities with science, technology, engineering, arts and mathematics.

The main questions were:

* Did children's eco-anxiety scores change from before to after the programme within each group?
* Did the programme group and the comparison group differ in eco-anxiety scores before or after the programme?

The study included 62 children in two existing classes. One class of 30 children participated in the Eco-STEAM programme, while the other class of 32 children continued its usual classroom instruction. The classes were not assigned randomly.

Children in the Eco-STEAM group participated in 18 activities over eight weeks, with three class periods on one day each week. Activities included observing nature, exploring the water cycle, making a windsors, building miniature ecosystem models and creating art with natural materials.

Children in both groups completed the nine-item Children's Eco-Anxiety Scale before and after the programme. The questionnaire asked about environmental worry, fear, sadness and related feelings. Scores were compared within and between the groups.
primary_outcomes: Change in Children's Eco-Anxiety Scale (CEAS-9) Total Score From Baseline to Post-intervention
title: Eco-STEAM Education and Eco-Anxiety in Primary School Children

brief_summary: This prospective, multicenter, randomized, non-inferiority controlled trial aims to compare the efficacy and safety of smart pressure-controlled flexible ureteroscopy and flexible ureteroscopy assisted by a distal flexible suction ureteral access sheath in patients with 2-3 cm renal stones. Eligible patients will be randomly assigned to one of the two treatment groups. The primary objective is to determine whether smart pressure-controlled flexible ureteroscopy is non-inferior to the suction sheath-assisted approach in terms of stone-free rate. Secondary outcomes include operative time, postoperative complications, intrarenal pressure-related outcomes, length of hospital stay, and other relevant perioperative parameters. The findings are expected to provide clinical evidence to guide the selection of surgical techniques for patients with 2-3 cm renal stones.
interventions: Distal Flexible Suction Ureteral Access Sheath-Assisted Flexible Ureteroscopy
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University
primary_outcomes: Immediate Stone-Free Rate
Postoperative Complication Rate
title: Comparison of Smart Pressure-Controlled Flexible Ureteroscopy and Flexible Suction Ureteral Access Sheath-Assisted Flexible Ureteroscopy for 2-3 cm Renal Stones

brief_summary:
This prospective, single-center pilot study will evaluate biologic augmentation during osteochondral allograft transplantation of the knee using a combination of bone marrow aspirate concentrate (BMAC) and Arthrex AlloSync Pure.

Approximately 10 adults undergoing osteochondral allograft transplantation for focal osteochondral defects of the medial or lateral femoral condyle will be enrolled. During surgery, BMAC will be collected from the tibial tubercle and mixed with Arthrex AlloSync Pure. The mixture will be applied to the recipient socket and graft plug before allograft implantation.

The primary objective is to assess osteochondral allograft incorporation using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) at 6 months after surgery. Secondary outcomes include MRI-based graft incorporation at 12 weeks and, when clinically indicated, 12 months; knee function and pain measured using the Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS) and Visual Analog Scale (VAS); radiographic graft healing; and postoperative complications and adverse events during one year of follow-up.
primary_outcomes: Osteochondral Allograft Incorporation Assessed by MRI
title: Biologic Augmentation of Osteochondral Allograft Transplantation in the Knee

To compare the frequency of adverse effects of statin therapy between patients receiving a fixed-dose regimen and those managed with a treat-to-target approach.

brief_summary:
Background: Intentional weight loss via various treatments results in a loss of lean mass of approximately 10% for every 10 kg of total weight lost. There is a paucity of data regarding changes in skeletal muscle mass associated with the novel anti-obesity drugs becoming available-specifically concerning not only quantitative changes but also the potential impact on muscle strength and the ability to perform activities of daily living.

Objectives: 1) To determine changes in body composition in individuals with obesity treated with semaglutide or tirzepatide for a period exceeding 6 months. 2) To analyze the impact of these changes on muscle strength and function.

Methodology: A prospective, multicenter study coordinated by the Obesity Section of the Spanish Society of Endocrinology and Nutrition (SEEN). The study includes individuals with obesity (without diabetes) undergoing pharmacological treatment with semaglutide or tirzepatide. Body composition is analyzed via bioimpedance before and after treatment. Muscle strength is assessed using handgrip dynamometry and the chair-stand test. Exploratory analyses cover weight loss percentage, weight loss categories, changes in fat mass and fat-free mass (kg and %), and estimates of total and appendicular skeletal muscle mass. Optional sub-studies include abdominal ultrasound (to measure subcutaneous and preperitoneal adipose tissue thickness) and ultrasound of the rectus femoris muscle. Data on side effects, diet, exercise, and quality of life are also recorded. Planned analyses include weight loss percentages, changes in variables following pharmacological treatment, adjustments for confounding variables (age, sex, protein intake, structured physical activity, etc.), and exploratory uni- and multivariate logistic regression analyses.
primary_outcomes: Sarcopenia
Percentage of total weight loss (TWL)
title: Changes in Body Composition Following Pharmacological Treatment for Obesity.

brief_summary: This retrospective study reviews existing medical records. No new treatments or tests are given. The study asks how well immunotherapy worked for people with a rare cancer called neuroendocrine carcinoma of the cervix. Immunotherapy is a treatment that helps the body's immune system fight cancer. The investigators will review the records of approximately 150 participants treated with immunotherapy for this cancer. The study will evaluate: (1) how long participants lived without the cancer getting worse; (2) how long participants lived overall; (3) whether the cancer shrank or stopped growing; (4) what side effects occurred, especially immune-related side effects; and (5) whether certain tumor markers or different treatment plans made a difference. Participants will not be contacted or asked to complete any procedures. Only information already contained in medical records will be used. Names and other personal details will be removed to protect privacy. The study has been approved by the ethics committee at Peking Union Medical College Hospital. The results may help doctors choose the best treatment for patients with this rare cancer. Results will be shared in medical journals and at medical meetings. For patients and families: This study does not enroll new participants. Questions about this cancer or immunotherapy should be directed to a physician.
primary_outcomes: Progression-free survival
title: Immunotherapy in Neuroendocrine Carcinoma of the Cervix

brief_summary:
Background: The study of factors associated with diabetic heart disease (DHD), the leading cause of mortality in diabetes, represents an unmet need. Autoimmune diabetes in adults (AID) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) differ in pathophysiology, vascular complications, and autonomic impairment, with significant implications for DHD, which results from a complex interplay among coronary micro- and macro-vascular circulation, neuro-immune control, and myocardial damage.

Objective: To characterize the complexity of DHD and its determinants by comparing AID and T2D.

Methods: DHD will be studied in individuals with AID, T2D, and healthy controls matched for cardiovascular risk factors. Advanced echocardiography and cardiovascular magnetic resonance will allow high-quality assessment of the different components of DHD (such as cardiac geometry, performance, and contraction). To identify the determinants of DHD, cardiac study results will be correlated with autonomic dysfunction tests, markers of small fiber neuropathy, and laboratory assessments of metabolic alterations, cardiac autoimmunity, and the inflammasome. Furthermore, genetic susceptibility to autoimmune diabetes and pancreatic autoimmunity will also be evaluated and correlated with DHD
primary_outcomes: Difference between LADA and T2D in the distribution in the identified clusters of diabetic heart disease
title: Differentiating Heart Disease Between Adult-onset Autoimmune and Type 2 Diabetes
