brief_summary: Non-specific neck pain is a pain and discomfort in the cervical spinal area that arises without trauma, clearly identifiable pathological cause such as fracture infection, nerve root compression, inflammatory disease or serious structural abnormality. Frequent smartphone use in a pathological way forces the user to adopt a compromised posture, gradually resulting in changes to both the postural and musculoskeletal systems. The incidence of non-specific neck pain (NSNP) makes up approximately 25% of all outpatients in general clinics and 12-70% of the general population. According to symptom duration, Chronic non-specific neck pain is usually classified as pain lasting or recurring for \> 3 months. Techniques such as SNAG mobilization and thoracic manipulation may also improve posture and cervical biomechanics by restoring normal spinal mobility. The objective of this study will be to compare the effects of Cervical, Sustain Natural Apophyseal Glide with and Without Thoracic Spine Manipulation on Pain, Range of Motion and Neck Disability in Smartphone Users with Non-Specific Neck Pain. Study design will be randomized clinical trial. Evaluation will be done by using NPRS, NDI and smartphone inclinometer. Non-probability convenient sampling will be used and the subjects will be allocated to two groups by random allocation. Group A will receive cervical SNAG and thoracic manipulation along with conventional physiotherapy and Group B will receive cervical SNAGS alone with conventional physiotherapy. Both groups will receive 12 sessions for the period of 4 weeks. Measurements of all the outcome variables will be taken at baseline, 2nd and 4th week. Results will be analyzed by using SPSS 24
interventions: Cervical SNAGS and thoracic manipulation with conventional physiotherapy
Cervical SNAG Mobilization Alone + Conventional Physiotherapy
lead_sponsor: University of Management and Technology Lahore
primary_outcomes: NUMERIC PAIN RATING SCALE
The Neck Disability Index (NDI)
SMARTPHONE INCLINOMETER
title: Effects of Cervical SNAGs With and Without Thoracic Manipulation on Neck Pain and Disability in Smartphone Users

brief_summary:
Prolonged sedentary behavior and habitual poor posture often lead to asymmetrical muscular loading and restricted joint mobility, such as glenohumeral internal rotation deficit (GIRD). Traditional interventions primarily focus on passive, localized stretching. However, the human body functions as an interconnected kinetic chain, where the mobility of distal joints (like the shoulder) is heavily influenced by the axial alignment of the thorax and pelvis, as well as breathing mechanics.

This study aims to investigate the immediate effects of Postural Restoration Exercises (PRE)-which uniquely combine specific asymmetrical positioning with prolonged exhalation techniques-on pelvic alignment and shoulder mobility in healthy young adults. Using a dismantling design, participants are assigned to three groups: the Postural Restoration Exercise (PRE) group, the Positional Exercise (PE) group, and the Breathing Exercise (BE) group. By comparing these groups, the study seeks to isolate and clarify whether the restorative benefits stem primarily from limb positioning, breathing mechanics, or the integration of both. The ultimate goal is to provide evidence for a highly efficient, self-administered intervention to improve motor performance and reduce injury risk.
primary_outcomes: Change in Standing Pelvic Alignment
Change in Glenohumeral Internal Rotation Range of Motion
title: Immediate Effects of Postural Restoration Exercises and Breathing on Shoulder and Pelvic Mobility

brief_summary:
Postoperative headache is a common complication following endovascular coil embolization of intracranial aneurysms and may increase analgesic requirements, impair patient comfort, and contribute to hemodynamic instability.

The greater occipital nerve (GON) has anatomical and functional connections with the trigeminocervical complex, suggesting that greater occipital nerve blockade may modulate headache-related pain pathways. However, the effectiveness of prophylactic greater occipital nerve block in patients undergoing elective endovascular coiling of unruptured intracranial aneurysms remains uncertain.

This prospective, randomized, sham-controlled, single-center clinical trial aims to investigate whether preoperative ultrasound-guided bilateral greater occipital nerve block reduces postoperative headache intensity during the first 24 hours following endovascular coil embolization.

A total of 76 patients will be randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive either ultrasound-guided bilateral greater occipital nerve block with 0.25% bupivacaine or bilateral superficial sham injections with 0.9% normal saline.

The active intervention will consist of 3 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine administered on each side in the fascial plane between the semispinalis capitis and obliquus capitis inferior muscles. The control intervention will consist of a superficial subcutaneous injection of 0.5 mL of 0.9% normal saline on each side.

All participants will receive standardized general anesthesia and postoperative multimodal analgesia.

The primary outcome will be the time-weighted average resting pain score during the first 24 postoperative hours, calculated from the area under the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) pain score-time curve.
interventions: Ultrasound-Guided Bilateral Greater Occipital Nerve Block
primary_outcomes: Time-Weighted Average Resting Pain Score During the First 24 Postoperative Hours
title: Effect of Bilateral Greater Occipital Nerve Block on Headache After Intracranial Aneurysm Coiling

brief_summary:
This is a multicenter, open-label, randomized, phase 3 superiority trial. The purpose is to find out whether a risk-adapted segmental esophagus-sparing radiotherapy plan is better than a standard radiotherapy plan at reducing moderate or worse acute radiation esophagitis in adults with locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who are receiving definitive concurrent or sequential chemoradiotherapy, with or without immunotherapy. Acute radiation esophagitis is inflammation of the esophagus caused by radiation; it can cause swallowing pain or difficulty and may interrupt treatment. The study will also check whether the esophagus-sparing plan affects tumor control, survival, other side effects, and quality of life.

About 140 participants will be randomly assigned 1:1 to the esophagus-sparing plan or the standard plan. Randomization will be stratified by study center, concurrent versus sequential chemoradiotherapy, ECOG performance status, and PD-L1 expression. In the esophagus-sparing group, the radiotherapy plan sets graded average dose limits to parts of the esophagus near the tumor target, based on how much the target overlaps the esophagus. The standard group receives routine intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) or volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) without active esophagus avoidance. Both groups receive the same radiotherapy dose (60-66 Gy in 30-33 fractions) and the same chemotherapy/immunotherapy chosen by their doctors. The study is open-label, so participants and doctors will know which radiotherapy plan is used; the main statistical analysis will be blinded to group assignment.

The main measure is the proportion of participants with Grade 2 or higher acute radiation esophagitis within 3 months after starting radiotherapy, graded by CTCAE v5.0. Participants will be followed for up to 24 months after randomization. This study does not test a new drug or device.
interventions: Standard IMRT/VMAT Without Active Esophageal Avoidance
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Grade 2 or Higher Acute Radiation Esophagitis (CTCAE v5.0)
title: Risk-Adapted Segmental Esophagus-Sparing Radiotherapy for Definitive Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to investigate whether using a Virtual Reality (VR) headset can help young people relax during the placement of an epidural catheter for pain control after pectus surgery.

An epidural catheter is a thin tube that is inserted by the anesthesiologist between two vertebrae in the back. Many teenagers experience anxiety or stress during the placement of this catheter.

To help reduce anxiety, medication called Midazolam can be given through an IV line. However, this does not always provide enough relief. Scientific studies have shown that virtual reality (VR) can help reduce anxiety, stress, and pain during medical procedures. By focusing on a virtual environment, patients are less aware of the procedure itself. In particular, VR has been shown to be a safe and effective way of improving comfort for children and adolescents during medical examinations and treatments.

A total of 78 adolescents aged 13 to 19 years will participate in this study. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups, each consisting of 39 participants:

Children in the interventional group will wear a VR headset during the placement of the epidural catheter. If the child still experiences significant anxiety or stress during the procedure, Midazolam will be administered through the IV line.

Children assigned to the control group will receive the usual care. This means that Midazolam will be given through the IV line if your child experiences significant anxiety or stress. Children in this group will not receive a VR headset.
primary_outcomes: Postprocedural anxiety score
title: Virtual Reality to Reduce Anxiety During Thoracic Epidural Placement.

brief_summary: Artificial intelligence is a rapidly developing technology in today's digital age and has had transformative effects in many areas, from education to healthcare. The use of AI in education offers personalized learning experiences and interactive learning environments by introducing new approaches to learning processes . This environment aims to take advantage of the opportunities offered by AI in nursing education to improve students' professional knowledge and skills and prepare them for future healthcare environments. Nursing processes, a fundamental component of nursing education, help nurses develop clinical decision-making, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills by enabling a systematic and holistic approach to patient care . However, traditional teaching methods may sometimes be insufficient to effectively support students in learning and applying these complex processes . The integration of artificial intelligence into nursing processes can help students acquire these essential skills more effectively and efficiently. Advanced language processing models such as ChatGPT provide nursing students with an interactive learning environment to analyze complex clinical scenarios, identify appropriate nursing diagnoses, and create personalized care plans . Previous studies investigating the integration of chatbot-based or AI-powered tools in nursing education have predominantly used non-experimental, descriptive, or quasi-experimental designs . These studies have generally reported improvements in students' critical thinking, learning motivation, and attitudes toward technology; however, they have tended to focus on a single outcome. Considering these shortcomings, the present study aimed to evaluate the effect of ChatGPT training in the nursing process on the perception of nursing diagnoses and critical thinking of final year nursing students using ChatGPT in the nursing process, within the framework of a randomized controlled trial.
primary_outcomes: Nursing Diagnoses Perception Scale score
title: The Effect Of Chatgpt Use By Final Year Nursing Students in The Nursing Processes On Their Understanding Of Nursing Diagnoses And Critical Thinking Skills

brief_summary: Runner's knee, most common condition causing knee pain; is defined by pain around or behind patella in young and physically active individuals. Runner's knee affects 25 to 40% knee patients reported in sports clinic. Exact pathology is unknown but factors such as trauma, overuse, muscular imbalance and maltracking of patella may be involved in causing symptom of runner's knee may continue to increase over years if unmanaged such as limitations in functional activities and poor quality of life. Patient suffering from runner's knee often shows weakness or inactivation of major muscles. A variety of different types of exercise have been explored to treat runner's knee, including neuromuscular training which restores movements by increasing strength, sensorimotor control and stability. However, in this research we will study McGill core and proprioception training effects on runner's knee patients. Objective of this study will be to compare effects of McGill core and proprioception training on balance, agility, deceleration and knee function in athletes with runner's knee. Study design will be randomized clinical trial. Evaluation will be done by using KUJALA, Star Excursion Test, Single leg stance Test, Agility T test and Functional Hop test. Non-probability convenient sampling will be used and the subjects will be allocated to two groups by random allocation. Group A will receive McGill core exercises and Group B will receive Proprioception exercises. Both groups will receive hot pack for 10 minutes as basic treatment of knee pain before techniques application. Both groups will receive 16 sessions for the period of 4 weeks. Measurements of all the outcome variables will be taken at baseline and 4th week. Results will be analysed by using SPSS 24.
lead_sponsor: University of Management and Technology Lahore
primary_outcomes: KUJALA
Star Excursion Test
Single leg stance
Agility T-test
Functional Hop Test
title: McGill Core and Proprioception Training in Runner's Knee.

brief_summary:
The goal of this parallel-group randomized controlled trial is to compare the effects of two different generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools (a video/audio interactive AI avatar versus a written AI learning assistant (chatbot)) on patient counseling skills self-assessment levels and instructional materials motivation in undergraduate nursing students.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is there a difference in health services counseling skills self-assessment scores between nursing students using an interactive AI avatar and those using a written AI chatbot?
* Is there a difference in instructional materials motivation scores between nursing students using an interactive AI avatar and those using a written AI chatbot? Researchers will compare Intervention Group 1 (students interacting asynchronously with a video and audio interactive AI avatar) to Intervention Group 2 (students interacting asynchronously with a written AI chatbot) to see if the AI interaction channel (video/audio avatar vs. text chatbot) significantly impacts student counseling self-efficacy and learning motivation.

Participants will:

* Complete baseline pre-test questionnaires, including a Demographic Information Form, the Generative Artificial Intelligence Usage and Competence Scale, and the Counseling Skills Self-Assessment Scale.
* Conduct patient education and counseling practice over at least 2 to 3 asynchronous sessions using their assigned AI tool on a standardized clinical case scenario.
* Complete post-intervention questionnaires, including the Counseling Skills Self-Assessment Scale, the Instructional Materials Motivation Scale, and an Application Feedback Form.
primary_outcomes: Change in Counseling Skills Self-Assessment Score
Instructional Materials Motivation Score
title: The Effect of Two Different Generative AI Tools on Nursing Students' Patient Counseling Skills and Motivation Regarding Instructional Materials

brief_summary:
Good toothbrushing is important for keeping children's teeth healthy. Dentists commonly teach children how to brush their teeth using dental models or instructional videos. However, it is not clear whether one method helps children clean their teeth more effectively than the other.

The purpose of this study was to compare face-to-face toothbrushing instruction using a dental model with video-based instruction in children aged 7 to 9 years.

Children were randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group watched a video showing how to brush teeth using a dental model, while the other group received a face-to-face demonstration using the same model and toothbrushing technique.

After instruction, a plaque-disclosing tablet was used to make dental plaque visible on the children's teeth. Photographs were taken before and after the children brushed their teeth for two minutes. The researchers then compared how much plaque was removed in each group.

The main question was whether the two teaching methods differed in helping children remove dental plaque immediately after instruction.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Dental Plaque Removal
title: Comparison of Model-Based and Video-Based Toothbrushing Instruction in Children

brief_summary:
Being overweight can increase the risk of heart disease. PCSK9 is a protein that helps regulate cholesterol levels in the blood. Exercise may affect PCSK9 levels, but previous studies have reported conflicting results.

The purpose of this study is to determine whether a program combining aerobic exercise and resistance training changes blood PCSK9 levels in adults with overweight. The researchers will also examine changes in blood cholesterol levels and body composition.

A total of 42 adults aged 18-40 years with overweight will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group will participate in a supervised exercise program three days per week for eight weeks. Each session will last approximately 60 minutes and include aerobic exercise, resistance training, warm-up, and cool-down periods. The other group will continue their usual daily activities without participating in a structured exercise program provided by the study.

Blood samples and body measurements will be collected before the program, after four weeks, and after eight weeks. Participants will also record their usual food intake and physical activity during the study.

The researchers expect that the combined exercise program may reduce blood PCSK9 levels compared with maintaining usual daily activities. The findings may help improve understanding of how exercise affects cholesterol regulation in adults with overweight.
primary_outcomes: Change in Serum PCSK9 Concentration
title: Effects of Concurrent Training on Serum PCSK9 Levels in Adults With Overweight

brief_summary:
The qualitative phase of the study will consist of focus group discussions (FGDs) with patients, caregivers, and clinicians. The aim is to explore the most relevant aspects of the experience of patients with lung cancer during treatment, considering three interconnected dimensions: the biophysical dimension (physical health and symptom burden), the psychological dimension (emotional, cognitive, and behavioural wellbeing), and the social dimension (social roles, relationships, and contextual resources). The study will also investigate patients' preferences and experiences regarding symptom monitoring by the clinical team during treatment.

The first step will involve a literature review on patients' preferences and experiences with lung cancer symptom monitoring during treatment. Findings will be complemented by informal discussions with clinicians and patient representatives to ensure a comprehensive understanding of patients' priorities and to identify potentially overlooked aspects.

The next step will involve FGDs with patients, caregivers, and clinicians recruited at IEO. The FGDs with patients and caregivers will be conducted in two phases. In the first phase, three FGDs will be conducted with five patients each, together with one FGD involving five caregivers. The objective will be to generate a comprehensive list of relevant attributes related to the reporting of Patient-Reported Outcomes (PROs), Patient-Reported Experience Measures (PREMs), Clinical Outcome Assessments (COAs), and the monitoring of quality of life through telemedicine systems and Digital Health Technologies (DHTs).

In the second phase, two additional FGDs will be conducted: one with five patients and one with five caregivers. These discussions will focus on refining the initial list of attributes and identifying those considered most important by participants. At the end of this phase, the Nominal Group Technique (NGT) will be used to prioritise the attributes and establish the final list.

The prioritised attributes will then be compared, with the support of clinicians, with the evidence identified in the literature. This step will ensure that all relevant aspects have been addressed and that potentially important elements not sufficiently represented during the FGDs are considered.

Finally, a focus group with clinicians will be conducted to define the different levels of the selected attributes. The resulting attributes and levels will constitute the basis for the subsequent quantitative preference study, aimed at systematically assessing the relative importance of the different aspects of treatment experience, symptom monitoring, and quality of life from the perspective of patients and other relevant stakeholders.
primary_outcomes: Identification and prioritisation of attributes relevant to lung cancer treatment experience and symptom monitoring
title: Patient Needs and Preferences for NSCL Cancer Treatment Monitoring

brief_summary:
This study evaluated a smart preventive program designed to predict injury risk associated with environmental factors among male amateur football players in Jazan, Saudi Arabia. The program considered environmental conditions, including temperature and humidity, as well as individual factors related to training readiness and preventive practices.

A total of 120 amateur football players were included in the study and divided into an intervention group and a control group, with 60 participants in each group. The intervention group used the smart preventive program, while the control group received no intervention from the study program.

The program aimed to help players recognize potentially unsafe training conditions and follow preventive recommendations related to training timing and intensity, hydration, rest breaks, warm-up, stretching, and sleep and recovery.

The study compared injury risk scores and preventive practices between the two groups. Injury occurrence was also assessed during the study period. The findings may help inform the development of practical, technology-based approaches to injury prevention among amateur football players training in hot environmental conditions.
conditions: Sports Injury Prevention and Injury Risk Prediction Among Amateur Football Players
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Football-Related Injuries Recorded During the Study Period
title: Smart Program for Predicting Injury Risk Associated With Environmental Factors Among Amateur Football Players in Jazan

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if PDO thread embedding combined with Binh Vi tablets and Esomeprazole works better than Binh Vi tablets and Esomeprazole alone in treating gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) in adults.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does adding PDO thread embedding improve GERD symptoms more effectively?
* Does the combined treatment improve participants' quality of life?
* What adverse effects may occur during PDO thread embedding? Researchers will compare PDO thread embedding combined with Esomeprazole 40 mg and Binh Vi tablets to Esomeprazole 40 mg and Binh Vi tablets alone to evaluate symptom improvement, clinical response, quality of life, and safety.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to receive either PDO thread embedding plus Esomeprazole 40 mg and Binh Vi tablets, or Esomeprazole 40 mg and Binh Vi tablets alone.
* Receive treatment for 4 weeks. Participants in the PDO thread embedding group will receive 2 sessions, one every 2 weeks.
* Visit the clinic for treatment and checkups.
* Complete questionnaires about GERD symptoms and quality of life at the start of the study, at 2 weeks, and at 4 weeks.
lead_sponsor: University of Medicine and Pharmacy at Ho Chi Minh City
primary_outcomes: Change in Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease Questionnaire (GerdQ) Score From Baseline to Week 4
title: PDO Thread Embedding Plus Binh Vi Tablets for Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the performance of a self-monitoring system (Solsius SelfCare) to detect pre-ulcerative clinical abnormalities in adults living with type 1 or 2 diabetes at high podiatric risk (grade 3 according to French HAS guidelines) and a history of healed diabetic foot wound.

The main question it aims to answer is:

\- Can the Solsius SelfCare system detect pre-ulcerative foot abnormalities with a sensitivity of at least 80%, defined as the proportion of temperature threshold exceedances (≥ 2.2°C difference between symmetric plantar sites over 2 consecutive days) confirmed by a clinical abnormality identified by a podiatrist?

There is no comparison group. All participants will use the same device throughout the study.

Participants will:

* Wear the Solsius SelfCare connected insoles daily (except during sleep) for 12 months
* Receive a push notification on their smartphone if a temperature difference ≥ 2.2°C is detected between symmetric sites on both feet over 2 consecutive days
* Attend scheduled podiatric follow-up visits every 3 months (at M3, M6, M9, and M12)
* Attend an additional unscheduled podiatric visit within 24 hours after each temperature alert, to verify the presence or absence of a pre-ulcerative clinical abnormality
* Complete a self-questionnaire after each temperature alert and a usability questionnaire (System Usability Scale) at the end of the study
primary_outcomes: To evaluate the performance of a self-monitoring system for detecting pre-ulcerative lesions in people living with stage 3 diabetic foot disease.
title: Continuous Monitoring of Plantar Temperature Variations Using Connected Insoles and a Mobile Application for Diabetic Foot.

brief_summary:
This pilot study aims to investigate the effects of a single oral dose of cannabidiol (CBD) on memory and attention in healthy adults aged 60 to 70 years. CBD is a naturally occurring compound found in cannabis that does not produce the intoxicating effects associated with THC.

The main research question is whether CBD can improve episodic memory (the ability to remember previously learned information), working memory (the ability to temporarily hold and use information), and attention compared with placebo.

The researchers hypothesize that participants will perform better on memory and attention tasks after receiving CBD than after receiving placebo.

The study will involve approximately 50 healthy adults aged 60 to 70 years. Each participant will attend two study sessions, scheduled 14 to 30 days apart. During one session, participants will receive a single oral dose of 25 mg CBD, while during the other session, they will receive a placebo capsule containing no CBD. The order of administration will be randomly assigned, and neither the participants nor the researchers assessing their performance will know which capsule was administered during each session.

Memory and attention will be evaluated using standardized memory tests and computer-based cognitive tasks. The findings will provide preliminary evidence on the potential effects of CBD on cognitive functioning in older adults.
primary_outcomes: Verbal Episodic Memory - RAVLT Delayed Free Recall
title: Effects of Cannabidiol on Memory and Attention in Adults Aged 60-70: A Pilot Study

brief_summary: This prospective, randomized, double-blind, controlled trial will compare the efficacy and safety of dexmedetomidine versus dexamethasone as adjuvants to bupivacaine in ultrasound-guided bilateral sphenopalatine ganglion block for adult patients (18-60 years, ASA I-II) undergoing elective functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS) under general anesthesia. Participants will be randomly allocated in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive bupivacaine alone, bupivacaine plus dexmedetomidine, or bupivacaine plus dexamethasone. The study will assess postoperative pain scores, duration of analgesia, total analgesic consumption, and intraoperative hemodynamic parameters, in addition to adverse effects.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Pain Intensity Assessed by the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS)
title: Dexmedetomidine Versus Dexamethasone as Adjuvants to Bupivacaine in Ultrasound-Guided Sphenopalatine Ganglion Block for Functional Endoscopic Sinus Surgery

brief_summary: This prospective clinical study will compare early healing and implant stability between two Nobel Biocare dental implant systems, NobelReplace S-TiUltra and NobelReplace CC TiUnite. Approximately 30 implants will be randomly assigned to one of the two implant groups and followed for 12 weeks after placement. Implant stability will be assessed using resonance frequency analysis at implant placement and at approximately 2, 4, 6, 8, and 12 weeks. Clinical healing, radiographic findings, and other treatment-related outcomes will also be evaluated during the follow-up period.
primary_outcomes: Mean Implant Stability Quotient (ISQ) Measured by Resonance Frequency Analysis (RFA)
title: S-TiUltra Implant Study

brief_summary: This clinical trial studies the feasibility, acceptability, appropriateness, and effectiveness of a remote screening and navigation program in increasing clinical trial enrollment among patients with prostate and bladder cancer receiving cancer care in the community setting. Genitourinary (GU) cancers, including prostate and bladder cancer, are among the most common affecting patients in the United States. In spite of recent advances, there are still only a few broad categories of treatments effective in both prostate and bladder cancer, and investigating new therapies in clinical trials is essential. In Washington State, the majority of patients with prostate and bladder cancer are treated at local community oncology sites. Patients are referred to Fred Hutch (FH) GU oncologists for clinical trials, but often this referral occurs once a patient has exhausted all standard of care options for treatment. This remote screening and navigation study involves approaching patients at community oncology and urology clinics in the Washington State area and pre-screening them for eligibility in open clinical trials at FH. Interested eligible patients will then be referred to our patient navigation program to be seen by a GU medical oncologist at Fred Hutch Cancer Center. This program may help increase access to clinical trials for patients with prostate and bladder cancer, as well as strengthen collaboration between community oncology providers and GU oncology specialists at FH.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of patients who "agree" or "completely agree" in the Feasibility of Intervention Measure (Feasibility)

brief_summary:
This pilot study is testing whether a special type of ultrasound called contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) can help detect if pancreatic cancer has come back after surgery.

People may be eligible to participate if they had surgery to remove pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) from the head or body of the pancreas and are currently being monitored for cancer recurrence using CT scans.

The study plans to enroll 10 participants: 5 people whose cancer has returned and 5 people whose cancer has not returned, based on their standard medical imaging results. Participants will not be randomly assigned to groups.

Researchers will use a Logiq E10 ultrasound machine with CEUS technology to perform an ultrasound examination of the area where the surgery was performed. The goal is to determine whether CEUS can be a practical and useful tool for identifying local pancreatic cancer recurrence.
primary_outcomes: Presence of Contrast Enhancement in the Pancreatic Surgical Site on CEUS
title: The Use of Contrast Enhanced Ultrasound (CEUS) In Post-Surgical Pancreatic Cancer Patients to Evaluate Local Disease Recurrence

The study will assess the strength and durability of therapeutic effects in a double-blind, parallel-design, placebo-controlled, two-center randomized controlled trial (RCT) comparing a single 25mg oral 'high' dose of psilocybin to a single 5mg oral 'low dose psilocybin (active placebo), both delivered in conjunction with a psychotherapy platform.

Participants will complete 5 study sessions: one sign-up session and four testing \& intervention sessions. Total participation will take about 18 hours. During the sign-up session, researchers will: discuss study details, review the participant's health history to make sure that it is safe for them to participate, perform tests to ensure that the participant meets the study criteria, and collect the participant's demographic information. During each testing \& intervention session, the participant will receive a different type of tES. Before and after getting tES, they will take part in tests that measure their brain activity and the strength, sensation, and function of their right hand.
primary_outcomes: Change in brain activity
Change in brain connectivity

brief_summary:
This exploratory study examines changes in sleep patterns during a four-week auditory stimulation intervention in 30 adults with self-reported sleep difficulties.

Participants use an 18-minute programmed audio recording daily before sleep for four weeks. The recording combines natural environmental sounds, rhythmic sound components, and background noise. Listening volume can be adjusted to a comfortable level.

Sleep assessments are conducted at the beginning of the study, Week 2, and Week 4. Each assessment lasts 24 minutes and includes 3 minutes of silence before the audio, 18 minutes of audio, and 3 minutes of silence afterward. Brain activity, eye movements, and chin muscle activity are recorded to classify wakefulness and non-rapid eye movement sleep stages.

This study evaluates whether brainwave audio intervention can improve sleep in people with sleep disturbances. Participants listen to the study audio, and their sleep is assessed before and after the intervention to examine changes in sleep patterns.
primary_outcomes: Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS)
title: Effects of Brainwave Audio on Sleep in People With Sleep Disturbances

brief_summary:
This project aims to identify immunobiological mechanisms underlying the development of depression during the perimenopause. During the perimenopause, the risk for recurrence of depression is increased 13-fold among women who previously had depression. Moreover, perimenopause overlaps with the age span exhibiting the highest suicide rate for women. The perimenopause can last for several years and starts when estrogen and progesterone levels begin to fluctuate, gradually declining. Sex hormones are powerful modulators of the immune response and the investigators therefore propose that changes in lymphocytes play a central role in depression during this time. Notably, our previous work has demonstrated deficient regulatory T-cell responses in women with post- partum depression and identified a specific pro-inflammatory profile that predicts depression during pregnancy. Importantly, our new pilot data derived from women with severe depression in the perimenopausal age span reveals alterations in tryptophan metabolites that control T- cell responses as well as in the methylation of genes involved in T-cell fate and chromatin remodeling. Taken together, these data support the hypothesis that the perimenopausal hormonal shifts induce a pro-inflammatory state, regulated by chromatin modifications in T-cells, that triggers depression in vulnerable women.

To test this hypothesis, the investigators will enroll 180 perimenopausal women aged 40-55, approximately half with depression and half without a diagnosis of depression. All participants will complete psychiatric assessments and provide blood samples to measure sex hormones, inflammation and immune cell changes. Women with depression will be reassessed approximately eight weeks later to identify blood markers that change as depressive symptoms improve.

This project seeks to improve understanding of the biological mechanisms of depression during perimenopause and aid the development of predictive biomarkers and more effective treatments.
primary_outcomes: Inflammatory markers
thyroid status, hormonal status
glucose levels
hemoglobin levels
title: The Immunobiological Mechanisms of Depression in Perimenopause

brief_summary:
Although breakthroughs in the management of Parkinson's disease (PD) have emerged in recent decades resulting in better control in symptoms, majority of patients with PD are still living with various disabling motor and non-motor symptoms despite they are already receiving the best contemporary medical or surgical treatments available to them. There is obviously a need to develop additional treatment modality to further optimize the control of symptoms and/or slow the disease progression for patients having PD.

Vagus nerve stimulation (VNS), a type of noninvasive brain stimulation is believed to modify brain rhythms by modulating the nucleus of the solitary tract and locus coeruleus and other regions known to play a role in gait. Moreover, VNS may modulate inflammatory pathways and reduce oxidative stress, making it a potential disease modifying treatment approach for neurodegenerative diseases linked to neuroinflammation such as PD

Further study is warranted to explore the efficacy of non-invasive VNS for its effects on gait and other symptoms of PD as well as the anti-inflammatory effects.
primary_outcomes: Change of gait
Severity and progression of Parkinson's disease
Quantitative Gait Assessment
Cognitive status
Change in mood
title: Non-invasive Vagus Nerve Stimulation for Parkinson's Disease

The study will collect and analyze clinical and microbiological information from patients treated with either antibiotic as part of routine clinical care. brief_summary:
Dental education requires a high level of manual dexterity, fine motor skills, and hand-eye coordination to perform precise clinical procedures. The development of these skills is an important component of dental training. This cross-sectional observational study aims to compare hand function and fine motor skills between first- and fifth-year dental students.

A total of 60 dental students, including 30 first-year and 30 fifth-year students, will be included in the study. Participants' hand function and fine motor skills will be assessed using the Jebsen-Taylor Hand Function Test (JTHFT). The test consists of seven standardized tasks representing activities of daily living and will be performed separately with the dominant and non-dominant hands. Task completion times will be recorded in seconds.

The study aims to identify potential differences in hand function and fine motor performance between students at different stages of dental education.
primary_outcomes: Hand Function Assessed by the Jebsen-Taylor Hand Function Test
title: Comparison of Hand Function and Fine Motor Skills Between First- and Fifth-Year Dental Students

brief_summary: Beetroot juice is rich in dietary nitrate, a compound that may improve muscle function and exercise performance. In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study, participants will complete four experimental conditions involving different doses of beetroot juice (0, 6.4, 12.8, and 19.2 mmol of nitrate from active supplementation) in a randomized order. Each condition will consist of three 70-mL shots (210 mL in total), containing different combinations of nitrate-rich beetroot juice and placebo. Neuromuscular performance will be assessed through bench press exercises at different intensities, evaluating bar movement velocity and muscular endurance. Salivary nitrate and nitrite concentrations, perceived exertion, and potential side effects will also be assessed. The study aims to determine whether increasing doses of beetroot juice produce different effects on neuromuscular performance.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of Adolescent Self-Injury Intervention Skills Training (ASIST), a treatment program developed by the research team, compared with treatment as usual (TAU) in adolescents who engage in non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. How do the effectiveness and safety of ASIST compare with those of treatment as usual in adolescents with NSSI?
2. How are treatment-related changes in psychological, clinical, behavioral, and biological measures associated with treatment response?
3. Can machine learning techniques be used to predict treatment responses in adolescents with NSSI?

Researchers will compare adolescents receiving ASIST with those receiving TAU to examine changes in psychological, clinical, and behavioral characteristics before and after treatment. They will also examine changes in cortisol and beta-endorphin levels, as well as brain activity and functional connectivity during task performance, to explore potential mechanisms associated with treatment response.

Participants will:

1. Receive either ASIST or TAU.
2. Complete psychological, clinical, and behavioral assessments before and after treatment.
3. Undergo measurements of cortisol and beta-endorphin levels.
4. Complete tasks during brain imaging assessments to measure brain activity and functional connectivity.
primary_outcomes: Change in Self-Harming Behaviors as Assessed by the Self-Harm Inventory (SHI)

brief_summary: This clinical trial addresses the financial hardship among adolescent and young adult (AYA) survivors using the new Lessening the Impact of Financial Toxicity (LIFT) UP intervention. AYAs with cancer experience significant and prolonged disruption in their lives due to their diagnosis and are at greater risk of financial hardship than any other age group with cancer. For AYA patients, health insurance literacy - one's ability to make informed decisions about choosing and using health insurance - is likely an essential component of being able to navigate care and manage costs. A promising strategy for addressing AYA financial hardship is to streamline existing, successful interventions into a single multilevel intervention. More specifically, combining patient education from a health insurance literacy intervention called CHAT (Let's CHAT about health insurance), which helps to address the book knowledge with organization support and financial navigation from an intervention called LIFT, which addresses the experiential knowledge could yield positive outcomes for AYAs. The addition of LIFT UP to usual care may improve AYA access to financial resources and reduce medical costs and distress associated with financial hardship.
primary_outcomes: Change of financial hardship
Change in health insurance literacy
title: Addressing Financial Hardship in AYA Cancer Survivors Through the Use of the New LIFT UP Intervention

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to determine if consuming a nutritional supplement before surgery affects weight loss, inflammation, and muscle in people with head and neck cancer cachexia. We are doing this study to learn more about weight and muscle loss in people with cancer that does not improve with just eating more calories; this condition is called cancer cachexia. Nutritional drinks created with nutrients that may reduce inflammation and help balance the body's immune system may be a promising treatment for cancer cachexia.

Our primary question is if these nutritional interventions affect muscle function through the gut-liver-muscle axis, which can be thought of as a biological "three-way conversation." The gut digests food and hosts a microbiome (a community of bacteria), the liver processes these nutrients and filters toxins, and muscles use this energy. If one part struggles, it can affect the others, impacting overall energy, metabolism, and strength.

Our primary goal of this study is to determine feasibility and safety.
primary_outcomes: Study feasibility of nutritional interventions before head and neck cancer surgery.
Study safety of nutritional interventions before head and neck cancer surgery.
title: Gut-Liver-Muscle Axis in Cancer Cachexia

brief_summary:
Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by persistent difficulties in social communication and interaction, as well as restricted and repetitive patterns of behavior. Emerging evidence suggests that the cerebellum plays an important role in social cognition and behavioral regulation, and abnormalities in cerebellar structure and function may contribute to the pathophysiology of ASD.Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) is a non-invasive neuromodulation technique that may modulate neural activity and functional connectivity within brain networks associated with ASD. However, the therapeutic effects of individualized cerebellar-targeted rTMS in children and adolescents with ASD remain unclear. This study aims to investigate the efficacy and safety of individualized cerebellar-targeted rTMS guided by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in children and adolescents with ASD. Additionally, the study will explore the effects of rTMS on brain structure and functional connectivity.

This is a multicenter, single-arm, exploratory interventional study involving 120 participants aged 6 to 18 years who meet the DSM-5 diagnostic criteria for ASD. Participants will receive individualized cerebellar-targeted intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) guided by MRI-based neuronavigation for two consecutive weeks.Clinical assessments and MRI examinations will be conducted at baseline, week 2, and week 12. Clinical outcomes will be evaluated using the Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS), Repetitive Behavior Scale-Revised (RBS-R), and Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ). Adverse events associated with rTMS will also be monitored. Peripheral blood samples will be collected once at baseline for genetic testing and genotyping to characterize genetic variation among participants. The findings of this study may provide preliminary evidence regarding the feasibility, safety, and potential therapeutic effects of individualized cerebellar-targeted rTMS in children and adolescents with ASD.
interventions: Individualized Cerebellar-Targeted Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation
primary_outcomes: Change in Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS) Total Score From Baseline to Week 2
title: Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) for Autism Spectrum Disorder

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn how different types of influenza (flu) vaccines affect the body's immune response over time. Researchers want to understand whether receiving egg-based flu vaccines, cell-based flu vaccines, or a combination of both influences how the immune system responds to future flu vaccinations.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

1. Does a person's previous flu vaccine type affect their immune response to a later flu vaccine?
2. Do repeated vaccinations with the same vaccine platform or switching between vaccine platforms produce different antibody responses?
3. How do different vaccination histories affect flu-specific immune cells and protection against different influenza strains?

Participants will be randomly assigned to receive one of four vaccine combinations:

* Egg-based vaccine followed by egg-based vaccine
* Egg-based vaccine followed by cell-based vaccine
* Cell-based vaccine followed by cell-based vaccine
* Cell-based vaccine followed by egg-based vaccine Researchers will compare immune responses among these groups.

Participants will:

* Complete a baseline survey about demographics, vaccination history, medical history, and household information.
* Receive a first seasonal influenza vaccination (egg-based or cell-based, depending on random assignment).
* Provide blood samples before vaccination and several times afterward to measure immune responses.
* Receive a second study influenza vaccination approximately 3 months after the first vaccination.
* Continue providing blood samples after the second vaccination.
* Complete brief follow-up surveys about health changes, additional vaccinations, and influenza-like illness during the study.

Blood samples will be collected up to eight times during each study year:

1. Before or on the day of the first vaccination
2. About 1 week after the first vaccination
3. About 1 month after the first vaccination
4. About 3 months after the first vaccination (the second vaccination will be given at this visit)
5. About 1 week after the second vaccination
6. About 1 month after the second vaccination
7. About 3 months after the second vaccination
8. About 6 months after the second vaccination

Participants may be observed for approximately 15 minutes after vaccination, consistent with routine vaccination practices.

Prior to the second vaccination, participants will be evaluated for any reasons that might make vaccination unsafe or require postponement. Participants who are able to become pregnant will complete a urine pregnancy test before the second vaccination. Participants who are pregnant or have a positive pregnancy test will not receive the second study vaccination but may continue study follow-up activities, including blood collection and surveys.

Participation in each study year lasts up to 10 months. Participants may choose to continue participating annually for up to 7 years.

Blood samples and related study data may be stored in a secure research biorepository for future studies related to infectious diseases, immunology, vaccine responses, and other health conditions. Stored samples will be coded to protect participant privacy, and identifying information will not be shared without appropriate approvals and participant authorization
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Hemagglutination Inhibition (HAI) Antibody Geometric Mean Titers at 1 Month After the Second Vaccination
title: Impact of Egg-Based and Cell-Based Vaccine Platforms on Immune Responses to Repeated Influenza Vaccination

brief_summary: Mitochondria are important organelles that generate energy (ATP) in human and mammalian cells. Currently, there are more than 50 kinds of diseases known to be related to mitochondrial defects in Taiwan. The incidence of mitochondrial diseases is very rare, about 1/5,000 to 1/10,000. The abundancy of mitochondria riches to 100,000 DNA copies in one oocyte, and the threshold of DNA mutation rate to cause pathogenicity is usually greater than 70%. Since mitochondria are inherited maternally, the pathogenic mitochondrial DNA in oocytes could be removed by modern artificial reproductive technology (ART). By treating with mitochondria replacement therapy (MRT), here we use the spindle transfer, following artificial insemination, the ooplasm from healthy donor oocytes could be transferred into the oocytes of patients to remove defected mitochondria, therefore creating the opportunity to produce healthy offspring. Therefore, in order to further detect the carrying rate of mutated mitochondrial genes in patients with mitochondrial defects after MRT, we aim to detect the mitochondria mutation in germ cells of patients in order to improve the specificity and operation procedures of this therapy.
primary_outcomes: Mitochondria DNA heterogeneity
title: Investigation of the Treatment of Patients With Mitochondrial Defects by Assisted Reproductive Technology

brief_summary: The investigators hope to learn if lobular breast cancer can be identified using a special procedure called a positron emission tomography (PET) magnetic resonance image (MRI) scan, collectively a PET/MRI scan, that uses a radioactive imaging agent called Fluorine 18 fluoroestradiol (18F-FES). This procedure may be able to define the extent of disease more clearly than the standard of care breast imaging exams. 30 participants will be enrolled and be on study for up to 6 months.
