brief_summary:
Dental anxiety is common among patients undergoing root canal treatment and may negatively affect their experience during dental care. Audiovisual distraction, combining visual entertainment with sound delivered through headphones, may help reduce anxiety by redirecting patients' attention away from the dental procedure.

The purpose of this randomized clinical trial was to evaluate whether a ceiling-mounted audiovisual entertainment system could reduce dental anxiety and heart rate during root canal treatment in patients diagnosed with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis.

A total of 100 adult patients were allocated to two groups. Participants in the intervention group received root canal treatment while watching audiovisual entertainment on a ceiling-mounted screen and listening through headphones. Participants in the control group underwent conventional root canal treatment without audiovisual entertainment.

Dental anxiety and heart rate were assessed at four predefined time points during the treatment appointment. The study compared changes in these outcomes between the two groups to determine whether audiovisual distraction could improve the patient experience during endodontic treatment.
conditions: Symptomatic Irreversible Pulpitis and Post Operative Pain
primary_outcomes: Change in Dental Anxiety Assessed Using a Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
Change in Heart Rate During Root Canal Treatment
title: Effect of Audiovisual Distraction on Dental Anxiety and Heart Rate During Root Canal Treatment

brief_summary:
SWAP-CKM (SWitching to Appropriate Prescription in Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome) is a pragmatic, cluster-randomized clinical trial designed to evaluate whether electronic health record (EHR)-based alerts can improve medication prescribing among adults with cardiovascular, kidney, and metabolic (CKM) conditions.

The study will include all eligible adult patients receiving care within Kaiser Permanente Northern California (KPNC) who have CKM conditions and opportunities for therapeutic medication substitution. Fifteen service areas are randomly assigned to either an intervention group or a usual care group.

Clinicians in the intervention group will receive EHR-based Best Practice Advisories (BPAs) identifying opportunities to replace potentially inappropriate medications with guideline-recommended therapies. The intervention may also include audit-and-feedback reports to support medication optimization. Clinicians retain full discretion over treatment decisions.

The primary outcome is the proportion of eligible therapeutic optimization opportunities achieved at 9 months. Secondary outcomes include medication initiation and discontinuation, medication optimization at 18 months, and polypharmacy burden.
interventions: Real-Time EHR Prompts and Audit-and-Feedback Reports
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Therapeutic Optimization Opportunities Achieved
title: SWitching to Appropriate Prescription in Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome

brief_summary: Orthognathic surgery changes the skeletal framework of the upper airway, but its functional effect on sleep-disordered breathing remains poorly documented, particularly with respect to respiratory effort. This prospective, exploratory, single-center pilot study will describe changes in the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) and in respiratory effort burden (REMOV, percentage of total sleep time with increased respiratory effort) measured with the Sunrise mandibular jaw movement (MJM) home sleep monitoring device, from 1 month before to 6 months after orthognathic surgery (bilateral sagittal split osteotomy with or without Le Fort I osteotomy). Twenty-five patients aged 15 years or older, scheduled for orthognathic surgery as part of standard care at CHR Sambre et Meuse (Namur, Belgium) and screened positive for sleep-disordered breathing risk, will be included. Results will be used to generate hypotheses and to size a future confirmatory study.
interventions: Orthognathic surgery (BSSO with or without Le Fort I osteotomy)
Facial multidetector CT in natural head position
lead_sponsor: CHR Sambre et Meuse Site Meuse
primary_outcomes: Change in apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) measured by mandibular jaw movement monitoring
Change in respiratory effort burden (REMOV)
title: Orthognathic Surgery and Obstructive Sleep Apnea Assessed by Mandibular Jaw Movement Monitoring (SUNRISE-ORTHO)

brief_summary: Biliary tract cancer is a group of malignant tumors involving the intrahepatic bile ducts, extrahepatic bile ducts, and gallbladder. Early detection can be challenging because non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT), which is commonly performed in routine clinical practice, may provide limited information for identifying biliary tract cancer. This prospective study aims to clinically validate an artificial intelligence (AI) system for screening and detecting biliary tract cancer on NCCT images. The AI system will independently analyze eligible NCCT examinations and generate a patient-level risk score for biliary tract cancer. The study will evaluate the diagnostic performance of the AI system against a predefined clinical reference standard. The primary objective is to assess the ability of the AI system to distinguish patients with biliary tract cancer from those without biliary tract cancer using NCCT. Secondary objectives include evaluating sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value. The study is designed to evaluate the clinical performance and potential screening value of AI-assisted analysis of NCCT. Routine clinical care and clinical decision-making will not be replaced by the AI system.
interventions: AI-Assisted Biliary Tract Cancer Screening Using NCCT
primary_outcomes: Patient-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of the AI system for distinguishing biliary tract cancer from non-biliary-tract-cancer cases using non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT)
title: Prospective AI-Assisted Screening of Biliary Tract Cancer Using Non-Contrast CT

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate the feasibility, tolerability, and preliminary analgesic effects of individualized Precision Confidence Mapping-guided low-intensity focused ultrasound neuromodulation in adults with chronic pain.

Participants will undergo MRI and resting-state fMRI to identify an individualized SCAN-connected centromedian thalamic target. Participants will then complete two treatment arms in randomized order: focused centromedian thalamic low-intensity focused ultrasound and unfocused control low-intensity focused ultrasound. Each treatment arm includes five consecutive daily stimulation sessions, separated by a washout interval.

The primary outcome is change in daily pain intensity measured using Brief Pain Inventory pain intensity items. Secondary outcomes include pain-related symptoms, physical function, fatigue, sleep disturbance, depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, pain catastrophizing, pain vigilance, neuropathic pain features, feasibility, tolerability, adverse events, blinding integrity, and exploratory neuroimaging measures.
primary_outcomes: Change in Daily Pain Intensity
title: Focused Ultrasound Neuromodulation for Chronic Pain

brief_summary:
This single-arm pilot study evaluates whether an integrated six-month care pathway for women with persistent vestibular vulvar pain and suspected hormonally mediated vestibulodynia can be delivered as planned, and how participants and clinicians experience it.

The pathway brings existing clinical and supportive elements together in one coordinated sequence: a digital symptom questionnaire whose answers are organised by topic for clinician review, specialist pre-screening by a gynaecologist with expertise in vulvar pain, pelvic floor screening by an authorised pelvic floor physiotherapist, gynaecological assessment by the responsible investigator, individual clinical management, pharmacy coordination, optional home videos and psychosexual support, and follow-up.

Up to 35 women aged 18-45 in Denmark are followed for 24 weeks. The study measures pathway feasibility (consent, completion of pathway steps, handover times, retention, deviations) and acceptability (participant and clinician experience). It does not measure symptom change or treatment effect.
primary_outcomes: Recruitment
Retention at week 24
Completion of core pathway steps
Handovers within target intervals
Participant-rated clarity, coordination and manageability
Clinician-rated workflow usability
Willingness to choose or recommend the pathway
title: Integrated Care Pathway for Hormonally Mediated Vestibulodynia: a Feasibility and Acceptability Pilot

brief_summary:
The aim of this study is to learn how doctors treat a type of metastatic colorectal cancer in everyday medical practice. The study focuses on patients whose cancer started on the left side of the colon and does not have specific gene changes called RAS mutations (this is known as RAS wild-type disease). It will assess effectiveness of two common types of targeted treatments: anti-EGFR medicines, which block signals that help cancer cells grow, and anti-VEGF medicines, which block the growth of blood vessels that supply tumors.

This is a real-world study, not a clinical study. This means that researchers will look at what happens when patients receive the treatments prescribed by their own doctor as part of their usual healthcare treatment. In this study, researchers will use information derived and de-identified from cancer clinics across the United States (from the Flatiron Health Analytic Database).
primary_outcomes: First-Line Treatment Patterns
Real-World Overall Survival (rwOS)
title: Real-World Treatment Patterns and Effectiveness of Anti-EGFR- and Anti-VEGF-based Therapies in Left-sided RAS Wild-Type Metastatic Colorectal Cancer

brief_summary:
Sedentary behaviour (SB) is an independent cardiovascular risk factor that remains highly prevalent among individuals attending long-term cardiac rehabilitation (CR) programs, despite participation in regular supervised exercise. Although CR provides an ideal setting for promoting healthy lifestyle behaviours, evidence on tailored interventions specifically targeting SB in long-term CR programs remains limited.

This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a 6-month tailored behavioural intervention, supported by digital health tools, in reducing SB among adults attending a long-term phase CR program. Participants will be randomly allocated to either an intervention group (IG), receiving standard CR plus individualized behavioural counselling, digital prompts, and educational resources, or a standard care group (SCG) receiving usual CR and educational resources only.

The primary outcome is objectively measured daily sedentary time assessed using activPAL4 (h/day). Secondary outcomes include objectively measured physical activity (PA), body composition, cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular strength, health-related quality of life and other behavioural outcomes. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, 3, 6, and 12 months, according to the specific assessment schedule. The study aims to determine whether integrating a tailored behavioural intervention into routine long-term CR leads to sustained improvements in SB and related health outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Change in daily sedentary time (h/day)
title: Impact of a Tailored Digital Intervention on Sedentary Behaviour and Physical Health in Long-term Cardiac Rehabilitation Patients

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a structured swallowing exercise program compared with conventional swallowing exercises in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The study will assess changes in swallowing function, swallowing biomechanics, airway safety, and quality of life following the intervention.
primary_outcomes: Change in Hyolaryngeal Excursion from Baseline to Week 8
Change in Penetration-Aspiration Scale (PAS) Score from Baseline to Week 8
Change in European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-Head and Neck 35 (EORTC QLQ-H&N35) Score from Baseline to Week 8
title: The Effectiveness of Structured Swallowing Exercise Therapy in Patients With Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: An Assessment of Swallowing Function and Quality of Life

brief_summary:
This open-label, decentralized pilot study evaluates the effects of daily chromium picolinate supplementation (8 mg providing 1,000 mcg chromium) for 8 weeks on appetite, food cravings, and food-related intrusive thoughts ("food noise"). The study aims to enroll up to 110 evaluable healthy adults aged 35-70 years with a body mass index (BMI) between 25 and 31 kg/m². Participants are stratified into two cohorts: those without prior Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist exposure (Cohort 1, n=80) and those with prior GLP-1 exposure following a 14-to-90-day washout period (Cohort 2, n=30).

Conducted entirely remotely via the Chloe mobile app, the study utilizes validated questionnaires (Food Cravings Questionnaire \[FCQ-T\], RAID-FN food noise inventory, appetite Visual Analogue Scales \[VAS\]), continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), daily meal logs, and weekly adverse event surveys to assess metabolic, behavioral, and subjective outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Impact on hunger and cravings after taking Chromium Picolinate daily
title: An Open Label Pilot Study Assessing the Impact of Chromium Picolinate Supplementation on Appetite and Cravings in Overweight Individuals

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether taurine supplementation, alone or combined with high-intensity interval training (HIIT) performed in morning or evening, affects circadian clock gene expression and inflamatory markers in adult women with obesity. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is the modulation of circadian clock gene expression associated with the anti-inflammatory effects of taurine?
* Does the timing of HIIT (morning or evening) affect circadian clock gene expression and inflammatory and metabolic responses? Researchers will compare six groups to evaluate the effects of taurine supplementation, HIIT performed in the morning or evening, and their combination.

Participants will:

* Take taurine (3g/day) or a matching placebo for 12 weeks, according to their assigned group;
* Perform HIIT in the morning or evening if assigned to an exercise group;
* Attend study visits at baseline (week 0) and after 12 weeks for assessments of metabolic and inflammatory parameters, circadian clock gene expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), as well as anthropometric measures, body composition and cardiorrespiratory fitness.
primary_outcomes: Changes in diurnal variation of BMAL1 gene expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs)
title: Effects of Taurine Supplementation and Morning or Evening High-intensity Exercise on Circadian Clock Genes and Inflammatory Parameters in Adult Women With Obesity

brief_summary:
Third-generation aromatase inhibitors (AIs) represent a standard adjuvant endocrine treatment for postmenopausal and high-risk premenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive early breast cancer. However, aromatase inhibitor-associated musculoskeletal syndrome (AIMSS)-characterized by joint pain, stiffness, and reduced mobility-occurs in approximately 50% of patients and significantly impairs treatment adherence and patient quality of life. Poor adherence to endocrine therapy is associated with reduced overall survival.

The purpose of this prospective, randomized (1:1), open-label, parallel-group clinical trial is to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and duration of therapeutic relief of acupuncture in managing AI-induced musculoskeletal symptoms in female patients with early-stage breast cance. A total of 200 participants experiencing AI-related joint pain are randomized either to receive 10 weekly 20-minute sessions of manual acupuncture over 10 weeks or to a control group receiving standard care without acupuncture. Joint pain severity, upper limb muscle strength and dexterity, sleep quality, and psychological distress are evaluated using validated patient-reported outcomes (Brief Pain Inventory \[BPI\], Rheumatoid Arthritis Pain Scale \[RAPS\], Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index \[PSQI\], and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale \[HADS\]) as well as objective physical performance tests (Hand Grip Strength Test and Grip Ability Test) at baseline, 10 weeks, 14 weeks (4 weeks post-intervention), and 22 weeks (3 months post-intervention).
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Musculoskeletal Pain Severity Score as Assessed by the Brief Pain Inventory Short Form (BPI-SF)
Change from Baseline in Upper Limb Muscle Strength as Assessed by the Hand Grip Strength Test (HGS)
Change from Baseline in Musculoskeletal Pain Severity Score as Assessed by the Rheumatoid Arthritis Pain Scale (RAPS)
Change from Baseline in Finger Dexterity and Hand Function as Assessed by the Grip Ability Test (GAT)
title: AKU Study - Acupuncture for Aromatase Inhibitor-Induced Musculoskeletal Syndrome

brief_summary: This phase II trial tests how well polatuzumab vedotin, mosunetuzumab, and acalabrutinib work in treating patients with mantle cell lymphoma. Polatuzumab vedotin is a monoclonal antibody, called polatuzumab, linked to a drug called monomethyl auristatin E. Polatuzumab is a form of targeted therapy because it attaches to specific molecules (receptors) on the surface of cancer cells, known as CD79B receptors, and delivers monomethyl auristatin E to kill them. Mosunetuzumab is a monoclonal antibody that may interfere with the ability of cancer cells to grow and spread. A monoclonal antibody is a type of protein that can bind to certain targets in the body, such as molecules that cause the body to make an immune response (antigens). Acalabrutinib is in a class of medications called kinase inhibitors. It blocks a protein called BTK, which is present on B-cell (a type of white blood cells) cancers such as mantle cell lymphoma at abnormal levels. This may help keep cancer cells from growing and spreading. Giving polatuzumab vedotin, mosunetuzumab, and acalabrutinib together may be an effective treatment option for patients with mantle cell lymphoma.
interventions: FDG-Positron Emission Tomography and Computed Tomography Scan
primary_outcomes: Positron emission tomography complete response (CR) rate
title: Polatuzumab Vedotin, Mosunetuzumab, and Acalabrutinib for the Treatment of Mantle Cell Lymphoma, PAcMan Trial

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to assess the effectiveness and safety of switching to bictegravir/lenacapavir (BIC/LEN) fixed-dose combination (FDC) compared with continuing stable baseline regimens (SBR) in virologically suppressed people with HIV.

The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the efficacy of switching to BIC/LEN (75/50 mg) fixed-dose combination (FDC) tablets versus continuing their stable baseline regimen (SBR) in virologically suppressed people with HIV.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants With HIV-1 Ribonucleic Acid (RNA) ≥ 50 Copies/mL at Week 24, as Determined by the United States (US) Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Snapshot Algorithm
title: Study of BIC/LEN FDC Versus Stable Baseline Regimens in Virologically Suppressed People With HIV

brief_summary:
Stroke is a leading global cause of death and disability. In 2021 there were 11.9 million incident strokes (10.7-13.2 million) and 93.8 million prevalent stroke survivors (89.0-99.3 million) worldwide. The burden in China is particularly severe: stroke is the leading cause of disability-adjusted life years lost, at 45.9 million, and causes more than 2 million deaths each year. Recurrence is common after a first stroke, with reported recurrence rates ranging from 5.7% to 51.3%; approximately 7.7% of patients recur within 3 months and 10.4% within 12 months, and a cohort study of 500,000 Chinese adults found that 41% (95% CI 41%-42%) of stroke survivors had a recurrence at 5 years. Recurrent stroke is associated with higher mortality, greater disability and increased consumption of health care resources, making secondary prevention after stroke the core element of reducing recurrence and improving prognosis.

Current stroke prevention and control systems remain largely reactive. Monitoring relies mainly on the patient's subjective perception after symptom onset, emergency response is triggered by telephone calls, and there is no mechanism for pre-symptomatic active sensing or active intervention at onset. The median onset-to-door time in China is still 180-240 minutes and reperfusion treatment rates (2.4%-7%) lag behind those of developed countries. Existing risk assessment tools such as the Framingham score are static models based on demographic characteristics; they cannot reflect the spatiotemporal evolution of physiological parameters in the 24-72 hours before onset and therefore cannot detect a 'recent high-risk state'. Digital health management is mostly one-way information push without bidirectional, agent-driven interaction, resulting in low patient adherence and warning messages that rarely translate into protective action.

Wearable health-monitoring devices combined with agentic artificial intelligence offer continuous, real-time and quantifiable physiological monitoring in everyday life. However, the effectiveness, feasibility and safety of such warning and intervention systems for stroke patients, especially for secondary prevention after discharge, have not been systematically evaluated. This study therefore evaluates a stroke early-warning system based on wearable monitoring and clinical data fusion, in order to provide evidence for a digital management model for stroke prevention.
primary_outcomes: Occurrence of stroke events
title: Integrating Wearable Monitoring and Clinical Data for Stroke Early Warning

brief_summary: RETAIN-3 is a phase II study in patients with cT2-T3N0M0 muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma of the bladder. Participants will receive neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab followed by clinical and biomarker-based assessment to inform subsequent treatment management.
primary_outcomes: 2-Year Metastasis-Free Survival (MFS)
title: Risk-Enabled Therapy After Initiating EV/Pembro for Bladder Cancer

brief_summary:
Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is one of the most common chronic complications of diabetes mellitus and a major cause of lower extremity pain, numbness, sensory loss, balance disturbance, diabetic foot ulcer and amputation. Painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (PDPN) is characterized by burning, stabbing or electric-shock pain, accompanied by numbness, paresthesia and sleep disturbance. Current treatments including glycemic control, neurotrophic agents and analgesics such as pregabalin and duloxetine only provide limited pain relief with adverse effects, and cannot effectively improve numbness or restore nerve function.

Secondary peripheral nerve entrapment induced by nerve edema contributes to the progression of DPN. Peripheral nerve decompression can relieve nerve compression, improve nerve blood supply and alleviate pain and numbness, and reduce the risk of foot ulcer and amputation. However, numbness may not be fully relieved in some patients after decompression alone, due to chronic nerve injury. Peripheral nerve stimulation (PNS), a targeted neuromodulation technique, can modulate abnormal nerve discharge and reduce peripheral sensitization, which may further improve pain and sensory abnormalities. To date, there are limited studies evaluating combined peripheral nerve decompression plus PNS for PDPN.

This study aims to evaluate the safety and efficacy of combined peripheral nerve decompression and peripheral nerve stimulation compared with peripheral nerve decompression alone in patients with painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy. The primary objective is to explore whether the combined therapy yields superior pain relief and recovery of nerve function, to provide new clinical evidence for individualized treatment of PDPN.
primary_outcomes: Change in Toronto Clinical Scoring System (TCSS) total score from baseline to 3 months after surgery
title: Safety and Effect of Peripheral Nerve Decompression Combined With Peripheral Nerve Stimulation for Painful Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy

brief_summary:
This is a randomized, evaluator-blinded, parallel group, comparator-controlled, multicenter study to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of GP0112 for cheek augmentation and correction of midface contour deficiencies.

Approximately 326 subjects will be randomized (1:1) to either treatment with GP0112 or Juvéderm Voluma XC(also known as Juvéderm Voluma with lidocaine).
primary_outcomes: Responder rate based on the Blinded Evaluators' live assessment using the Medicis Midface Volume Scale (MMVS).
title: A Study to Evaluate the Safety and Effectiveness of GP0112 for Cheek Augmentation and Correction of Midface Contour Deficiencies

brief_summary:
The primary purpose of this study is to evaluate the development and efficacy of an evidence-based kindness intervention. By focusing on university students in Islamabad, this research aims to determine whether a positive psychology intervention centered on practicing intentional acts, emotions and thoughts of kindness can serve as an accessible mental health tool. Ultimately, the study seeks to understand if this program can successfully enhance the psychosocial well-being of young adults navigating the unique psychological, social, and personal pressures of university life.

This study attempts to answer the following central question:

What is the impact and efficacy of a developed kindness intervention on the psychosocial well-being of emerging adults, particularly university students in Islamabad?
primary_outcomes: Psychosocial Wellbeing
title: This Study Tests the Development and Efficacy of a Kindness Focused Intervention on University Students in Islamabad. It Aims to See the Impact of This Intervention on the Psychosocial Well-being of These Emerging Adults.

brief_summary:
Inguinal hernias occur when abdominal contents, such as intestine or fat, protrude through a weakness in the lower abdominal wall. While most hernia repairs are scheduled electively, some hernias present as urgent emergencies due to incarceration (the contents become trapped) or strangulation (the blood supply to the trapped tissue is cut off). In emergency operations, synthetic mesh placement may be avoided due to the increased risk of surgical site infections, tissue swelling, or bowel contamination. In such settings, surgeons rely on tissue-based (mesh-free) repairs. The conventional Bassini repair is a standard non-mesh technique, but it can be associated with higher hernia recurrence rates. The Desarda technique is a physiological, mesh-free repair that uses an undetached strip of the patient's own external oblique aponeurosis (tendinous muscle tissue) to reinforce the weakened inguinal floor without tension.

The main objective of this study is to compare the surgical outcomes of conventional Bassini repair alone versus Bassini repair combined with the Desarda technique in adult patients undergoing emergency surgery for urgent, complicated inguinal hernias.

This prospective randomized controlled trial is conducted at the Department of General Surgery, Assiut University Hospital. A total of 70 eligible participants presenting with acutely complicated inguinal hernias will be randomly assigned to one of two equal groups:

* Group A (Bassini Repair): Patients undergo standard open emergency tissue herniorrhaphy alone.
* Group B (Desarda Repair): Patients undergo emergency herniorrhaphy combined with the Desarda aponeurotic reinforcement technique.

Participants are monitored during their hospital stay and will attend structured outpatient follow-up visits up to 12 months postoperatively. The primary outcome evaluated is the rate of hernia recurrence. Secondary outcomes include surgical site infections, seroma and hematoma formation, postoperative pain scores (using the Visual Analogue Scale), duration of operative procedure, hospital stay length, and time required to resume normal activities and return to work.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Inguinal Hernia Recurrence
title: Bassini Repair Versus Desarda Technique in Urgent Complicated Inguinal Hernia Repair

brief_summary: This was a randomized, parallel, double-blind clinical trial with healthy volunteers
primary_outcomes: Subjective pain
Pain tolerance
title: Single-dose Effects of Ayahuasca Compared to Esketamine on Experimentally Induced Pain

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate the efficacy and safety of recombinant enzymes contained in pbserum Plus® and pbserum HA 2.0® for aesthetic and regenerative tissue bioremodeling.

The study will include adult participants with clinical conditions such as facial or body skin laxity, localized adiposity, cellulite, tissue fibrosis, subcutaneous nodules, and pathological scars. Participants will be evaluated according to the specific clinical condition being treated.

The study will assess changes in the treated tissues using clinical evaluations, standardized photographs, patient and evaluator assessments, validated questionnaires, ultrasonography, elastography, cutometry, and three-dimensional imaging when applicable.

Participants will be followed longitudinally after treatment, with evaluations at different time points to monitor clinical changes, aesthetic outcomes, satisfaction, and safety. Possible adverse events and treatment-related complications will also be recorded throughout the study.

The study aims to determine whether recombinant enzyme-based treatments can provide clinical improvement while maintaining an acceptable safety profile and to generate scientific evidence regarding their use in aesthetic and regenerative medicine.
primary_outcomes: Clinical Safety
Change in Skin Elasticity Measured by Cutometry
Change From Baseline in Subcutaneous Fat Thickness Measured by Ultrasonography
Change in Treated-Area Volume
Change From Baseline in Cellulite Severity Scale Score
title: Prospective Evaluation of Recombinant Pbserum Plus® and Pbserum HA 2.0® in Aesthetic and Regenerative Bioremodeling

brief_summary:
This observational study aims to develop an integrated genomic and clinical database to support the discovery and validation of biomarkers for cancer diagnosis, treatment selection, and prediction of treatment response.

The study will include adults aged 19 years or older with diagnosed or suspected cancer, as well as consenting individuals undergoing routine health screenings at Samsung Medical Center. Researchers will collect residual tissue specimens obtained during routine diagnostic or therapeutic procedures and additional blood samples collected alongside routine clinical blood tests. Previously collected specimens from approved biobank resources may also be used.

Genetic, molecular, and protein analyses will be performed on the collected specimens, and the results will be integrated with clinical information, including cancer diagnosis, treatment history, treatment response, and disease outcomes. Patient-derived organoids and immune cells may also be used to investigate drug responses in laboratory models.

The study aims to identify biomarkers associated with cancer development, progression, and treatment response, and to support the development of diagnostic tools and personalized treatment strategies.

No experimental treatments will be assigned as part of this study, and no additional tissue biopsies will be performed solely for research purposes.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants with Integrated Genomic and Clinical Data
title: Development and Utilization of an Integrated Clinical Genomic Database

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether adding stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) or fractionated stereotactic radiotherapy (SRT), delivered on a linear accelerator (LINAC), to osimertinib improves control of brain metastases in adults with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) carrying a sensitizing EGFR mutation (exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R) whose brain metastases cause neurological symptoms (present at diagnosis or arising during osimertinib treatment). The main questions it aims to answer are:

* What proportion of participants achieve an intracranial objective response (complete or partial response by RANO-BM criteria)?
* How long do participants live without intracranial or overall disease progression, how long do they live overall, and what side effects occur with the combined treatment?

Participants will:

* Take osimertinib 80 mg by mouth once daily (or continue it if they have already started it).
* Receive SRS (1 fraction) or SRT (3 or 5 fractions) to all brain metastases (1 to 4 lesions, each 4 cm or smaller) at Cho Ray Hospital, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.
* Have brain MRI (or contrast-enhanced CT if MRI is not possible) and chest-abdomen CT every 12 weeks, monthly clinic visits to check for side effects, and blood tests, ECG and echocardiography every 12 weeks.
conditions: Brain Metastases From Non-small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)
primary_outcomes: Intracranial objective response rate (iORR)
Intracranial disease control rate (iDCR)
title: Osimertinib Plus Stereotactic Radiosurgery/Radiotherapy for EGFR-Mutant Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer With Symptomatic Brain Metastases

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate GN001 in adults aged 18 to 75 years with CD19-positive relapsed or refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma or B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. GN001 is an investigational lentiviral vector-based treatment designed to generate CD19-targeted chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells within the body.

The main purpose is to assess safety and tolerability at different doses. The study will also assess antitumor activity, the expansion and persistence of CAR T cells, and biological responses to treatment. Participants will receive GN001 by intravenous infusion. The study includes dose escalation and may include dose expansion after safety review. Long-term safety follow-up is planned.
conditions: Relapsed or Refractory B-Cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma
Relapsed or Refractory B-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
lead_sponsor: Department of Hematology,Rheumatology and Immunology,Pu'er People's Hospital
primary_outcomes: Incidence of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs)
title: GN001 for Relapsed or Refractory B-Cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma and B-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia

brief_summary: This multi-country, longitudinal follow-up study will enrol adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) who previously participated in the Phase III B-Well-1 ((202009: NCT05630807) or B-Well-2 (219288: NCT05630820) studies, received 24 weeks of Bepirovirsen treatment, and achieved hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) levels less than or equal to (\<=) 100 International units per millilitres (IU/mL) at Week 72 without achieving functional cure. No investigational treatment will be administered in this study. Participants will be followed approximately every 6 months for up to 4 years, and retrospective data will be collected from Week 72 of the parent study until enrolment. The study aims to evaluate the long-term durability of HBsAg suppression and disease-related outcomes. The study will end at the last visit of the last participant globally (Month 48). The primary objective of the study is to describe the long-term durability of HBsAg reduction in participants who achieved HBsAg levels ≤100 IU/mL at Week 72 following 24 weeks of Bepirovirsen treatment.
primary_outcomes: Time From B-Well Week 72 to Confirmed Loss of Response
title: B-Ensure: Long-term Follow-up Study to Evaluate Durability of Treatment Response in Previous Bepirovirsen Study Participants

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Endoscopic Radial Compression Gastroplasty (ERCG) in mitigating weight regain following discontinuation of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs). Approximately 60 adults with prior GLP-1 RA use and confirmed weight rebound after treatment cessation will be randomized 1:1 to either ERCG combined with Intensive Lifestyle Intervention (ILI), or ILI alone.

The primary outcome is the between-group difference in percent Total Body Weight Loss (%TBWL) from randomization to week 12; secondary outcomes include %TBWL at 24 and 52 weeks; changes in Body Mass Index (BMI), body composition, metabolic parameters (e.g., glycemic control, lipid profile), and quality of life; adherence to ILI; and adverse events, all assessed over 12, 24 and 52-week follow-up period. This study will generate preliminary evidence on the effectiveness and safety of ERCG as an intervention for weight regain after GLP-1 RA withdrawal, and the results will inform the design of future confirmatory trials, including sample size and endpoint selection.
lead_sponsor: Affiliated Hospital to Academy of Military Medical Sciences
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Total Body Weight Loss (%TBWL) at Week 12
title: ERCG vs Intensive Lifestyle Intervention for Weight Regain After GLP-1 RA Discontinuation

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a gamified neonatal initial care educational intervention on knowledge, clinical skills, and self-efficacy among undergraduate midwifery students.

Neonatal initial care requires appropriate clinical knowledge, practical skills, and timely decision-making. Gamification-based educational approaches may support active learning and provide opportunities to practice clinical decision-making in simulated environments.

The study is planned to include 68 undergraduate midwifery students at KTO Karatay University in Türkiye. Participants will be randomly assigned to an intervention group (n=34) or a control group (n=34).

Both groups will receive theoretical education on neonatal initial care. The intervention group will additionally participate in a hybrid escape room activity combining a web-based digital game with hands-on simulation using neonatal mannequins and clinical equipment. The control group will continue with conventional theoretical education without the additional gamified activity.

The primary outcome will be neonatal initial care clinical skills, assessed through an Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) before and shortly after the intervention. Secondary outcomes will include neonatal initial care knowledge and general self-efficacy, assessed at baseline, shortly after the intervention, and at one-month and three-month follow-up.

The study will examine whether adding a gamified hybrid escape room activity to conventional theoretical education improves learning outcomes among midwifery students.
interventions: Gamified Hybrid Escape Room-Based Neonatal Initial Care Education
Conventional Theoretical Neonatal Initial Care Education
primary_outcomes: Change in Neonatal Initial Care Clinical Skills Score
title: Effect of Gamified Neonatal Initial Care Education on Midwifery Students

brief_summary:
This is a multicenter, open-label, randomized phase III study in older or frail adults with unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who are considered unsuitable for concurrent chemoradiotherapy. All participants first receive standard induction chemotherapy plus immunotherapy (4-6 cycles), which is part of routine clinical care and not a study intervention. Patients whose cancer responds (complete response, partial response, or stable disease) may then sign informed consent and be randomly assigned 1:1 to receive either reduced-dose thoracic radiotherapy or standard-dose thoracic radiotherapy. After radiotherapy, both groups receive immune checkpoint inhibitor maintenance therapy for at least 6 months.

The main goal is to find out whether reduced-dose radiotherapy is not unacceptably worse than standard-dose radiotherapy in controlling the cancer at 1 year, measured by the 1-year progression-free survival rate. The study will also compare side effects, overall survival, tumor response, and treatment completion. About 276 patients will be enrolled at Ruijin Hospital and six collaborating hospitals in China.
primary_outcomes: 1-Year Progression-Free Survival (PFS) rate
title: Reduced-Dose vs Standard-Dose Thoracic Radiotherapy After Induction Chemoimmunotherapy in Older or Frail Stage III NSCLC

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of the fully closed loop (FCL) iLet automated insulin delivery (AID) System in people ≥18 years old with type 1 diabetes or type 2 diabetes requiring insulin therapy. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Do HbA1c levels decrease when using the iLet FCL algorithm?

What medical problems do participants have when using the iLet FCL algorithm?

Participants will use the iLet FCL for 13 weeks, undergo bloodwork, and complete psychosocial questionnaires.
primary_outcomes: HbA1c change from baseline
Rate of severe hypoglycemia requiring assistance to actively administer treatment
Rate of severe hypoglycemia resulting in seizure/loss of consciousness
Rate of hyperosmolar hyperglycemic syndrome (HHS) or diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)
title: Safety and Efficacy of the Fully Closed Loop iLet Bionic Pancreas in Adults With Type 1 and Type 2 Diabetes

brief_summary: This is a phase 1, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, single ascending dose study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics (PK/PD) of single oral doses of NTQ6179 tablets in healthy participants. A total of 56 healthy participants will be enrolled in 7 sequential dose cohorts, with an allocation ratio of NTQ6179 to placebo of 6:2 in each cohort.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs), treatment-related TEAEs (TRAEs), and serious adverse events (SAEs)
title: A Phase 1 Clinical Trial of NTQ6179 Tablets in Healthy Volunteers

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety of injecting a 2% chlorine dioxide solution directly into tumors in adults with advanced solid tumors, and to determine whether the injected solution stays within the tumor under real-time imaging guidance. Chlorine dioxide reacts with and destroys the tissue it contacts and is consumed locally within about a minute. Up to about 50 participants will receive up to 4 treatment sessions per lesion, about one week apart, and will be followed for 12 months.
primary_outcomes: Number of participants with dose-limiting toxicities
Number of participants with treatment-emergent adverse events
Number of participants with grade 3 or higher adverse events
Number of participants with serious adverse events
Number of participants with adverse events related to study drug
Percentage of deliveries with solution outside the lesion boundary
Percentage of deliveries terminated by a mandatory stopping rule
Number of participants with non-target tissue injury
title: Intratumoral Chlorine Dioxide Injection in Advanced Solid Tumors

brief_summary: This randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial evaluated the safety and efficacy of umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell (UC-MSC) secretome, given as an add-on to standard therapy, in women with Sjogren's syndrome. Twenty-nine participants were randomly assigned to receive six intramuscular injections of either UC-MSC secretome or 0.9% sodium chloride (placebo) over five weeks, while continuing their usual corticosteroid and/or immunosuppressant treatment. The main outcome was the change in disease activity measured by the EULAR Sjogren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI). Secondary outcomes were the inflammatory markers erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), and adverse events.
interventions: Umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived secretome
primary_outcomes: Change in EULAR Sjogren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI) score
title: Umbilical Cord Mesenchymal Stem Cell Secretome in Patients With Sjogren's Syndrome

brief_summary: A prospective, randomized, double-blinded controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy of a 2-week preoperative and 2-week postoperative course of oral dutasteride (0.5 mg daily) in reducing perioperative blood loss, irrigation requirements, and catheterization time in patients on anticoagulant therapy undergoing bipolar TURP for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).
conditions: Perioperative Hemorrhage Control During Bipolar Transurethral Resection of the Prostate (TURP) in Patients on Anticoagulant or Antiplatelet Therapy
primary_outcomes: Change in Hemoglobin (Hb) Level
Change in Hematocrit (Hct) Level
title: Perioperative Dutasteride for Hemorrhage Control in Bipolar TURP Under Anticoagulation.

brief_summary:
The purpose of this First-in-Human, Phase 1 study is to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), pharmacodynamics (PD), immunogenicity, and preliminary antitumor activity of MC001 in adults with advanced or metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and other solid tumors that have relapsed or are refractory to standard therapies. MC001 is an investigational dimeric antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) that targets folate receptor alpha (FRα) and delivers a microtubule-disrupting cytotoxic payload, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE).

The study will be conducted in two sequential parts:

Part A (Dose Escalation): Evaluates ascending intravenous (IV) dose levels of MC001 administered once every 3 weeks (Q3W) using a standard 3+3 design in patients with advanced solid tumors to identify dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs), the maximum tolerated dose (MTD), and the recommended dose for expansion (RDE).

Part B (Dose Expansion): Evaluates MC001 at the selected RDE in patients with advanced or metastatic PDAC whose tumors express FRα on at least 30% of tumor cells to further characterize safety and preliminary efficacy.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants With Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs) and Serious Adverse Events (SAEs)
Number of Participants Experiencing Dose-Limiting Toxicities (DLTs) in Part A (Dose Escalation)
title: A Study of MC001 in Patients With Advanced or Metastatic Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and Other Folate Receptor Alpha (FRα)-Expressing Solid Tumors

brief_summary: Knee arthroscopy is one of the most common orthopedic procedures, and effective postoperative analgesia is essential for early mobilization and patient comfort. Femoral nerve block provides effective analgesia after knee surgery but can cause quadriceps weakness. The anterior nerves of the knee (ANK) block is a recently described, motor-sparing fascial plane block targeting the sensory nerves of the anterior knee. This prospective, randomized, single-blind study compares ultrasound-guided ANK block with ultrasound-guided femoral nerve block in adult patients undergoing elective knee arthroscopy under spinal anesthesia, with respect to postoperative analgesic consumption, pain scores, intraoperative hemodynamics and time to first mobilization.
interventions: Anterior Nerves of the Knee (ANK) Block
primary_outcomes: Total Postoperative Tramadol Consumption
Pain Score at Rest
Pain Score on Movement
title: Anterior Nerves of the Knee Block Versus Femoral Nerve Block for Knee Arthroscopy

brief_summary:
This study compared two methods of making bases for upper complete dentures: three-dimensional (3D) printing and conventional heat curing. A denture base rests on the gums and supports the artificial teeth. The aim was to determine whether the manufacturing method affected retention, stability and support: how well the base resisted being dislodged, resisted horizontal or rocking movements, and resisted movement towards the supporting tissues under pressure.

Sixteen participants with no remaining upper teeth took part. Two denture bases were made for each participant from the same dental impression, one using each manufacturing method. The order in which the bases were tested was randomly determined by computer. The bases were labelled with codes so that two independent examiners were not informed of the manufacturing method. Each examiner assessed anterior and posterior retention, front-to-back and lateral stability, and front-to-back and lateral support using predefined rating scales. Scores were compared within each participant, and agreement between the examiners was also evaluated.
primary_outcomes: Anterior Retention of the Maxillary Denture Base
Posterior Retention of the Maxillary Denture Base
title: Comparison of 3D-Printed and Heat-Cured Upper Complete Denture Bases

brief_summary: This is a phase II study evaluating a novel combination therapy for untreated extensive-stage small cell lung cancer. The treatment involves an initial induction phase with the drug Adebrelimab plus standard chemotherapy and low-dose radiotherapy, followed by an Adebrelimab maintenance phase. The primary objective is to assess the efficacy of this approach in prolonging overall survival (OS) and to evaluate its safety in approximately 25 patients.
lead_sponsor: Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital
primary_outcomes: Overall Survival (OS)
title: Low-Dose Radiotherapy Plus Adebrelimab and Chemotherapy for Extensive-Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer

brief_summary: This is a prospective single-center, single-arm, feasibility trial designed to evaluate the safety of the HistoSonics Histotripsy System for treatment of renal tumors. The type of design is exploratory and is considered interventional. Following histotripsy, subjects will undergo imaging ≤ 72 hours post-index procedure. Additionally, subjects will be followed at 1 month, 3 months, 6 months and 12 months timepoints.
primary_outcomes: Primary technique efficacy
Primary safety endpoint
title: The Edison™ System for Treatment of Renal Tumors Using Histotripsy (Histo-Renal Trial)

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to learn whether connecting people at high risk for developing heart failure to a heart doctor (cardiologist) leads to greater use of treatments that can lower that risk. Heart failure is a condition in which the heart cannot pump blood as well as it should. The study focuses on Veterans living in rural areas, who often have a higher risk of heart failure and less access to heart care.

The study team will use health record information to find Veterans who are at high risk for heart failure but do not yet have it, and who have health factors that could be improved with preventive treatment. The study team expects that telling these Veterans and their primary care providers about the elevated risk, and offering early cardiology care, will lead to greater use of treatments known to help prevent heart failure compared with usual care.

The main questions the study aims to answer are:

* Does informing a Veteran and their primary care provider about the Veteran's elevated risk for heart failure, and offering a referral to a cardiologist, increase the use of treatments known to help prevent heart failure?
* Does having a care navigator reach out to Veterans and their primary care providers further help connect these Veterans to preventive care?

Veterans in the study will be placed by chance into one of three groups. One group will receive usual care. A second group, along with their primary care provider, will be told about the Veteran's elevated risk for heart failure and offered a referral to a cardiologist. A third group will receive that same information and referral offer, plus outreach from a care navigator who can explain more about heart failure and the reason for the referral, answer questions, and help with scheduling.
interventions: Notification and Cardiology Referral Plus Care Navigation
lead_sponsor: Palo Alto Veterans Institute for Research
primary_outcomes: New preventive treatments
title: Notification Of High-Risk Veterans for Access to Heart Failure Prevention

brief_summary:
Nocturnal scratching is a frequent and meaningful symptom in dermatological conditions such as atopic dermatitis. It may reflect underlying disease activity and can substantially disrupt overall sleep and quality of life. Existing approaches to characterizing Nocturnal Scratching-such as self-reports, sleep diaries, and video monitoring-are often subjective, labor-intensive, or lack scalability for widespread use.

Emerging wearable technologies offer an alternative, by enabling objective, continuous, and non- invasive signal related to scratch behavior during sleep.
primary_outcomes: Scratch boat measurements
title: Observational Analytical Validation Study of the Replior ScratchSense

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate whether High-flow Nasal Cannula Oxygen Therapy (HFNC) provides superior respiratory support compared to Conventional Oxygen Therapy (COT) in children with High-Altitude Pulmonary Edema (HAPE).
primary_outcomes: Proportion of treatment failure
title: High-flow Nasal Cannula Oxygen Therapy Versus Conventional Oxygen Therapy in Children High-altitude Pulmonary Edema

brief_summary:
This study will assess whether women with obesity and early estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer can complete 26 weeks of semaglutide treatment while continuing their prescribed hormone therapy for breast cancer. The researchers expect that semaglutide can be given alongside hormone therapy with good treatment adherence. The study will also examine side effects, weight changes, body composition, metabolic health and quality of life.

Thirty-two women will be randomly assigned to start semaglutide immediately or after a 26-week waiting period. Both groups will continue usual breast cancer care and receive written advice about diet and physical activity. Semaglutide will be self-injected under the skin once a week for 26 weeks, with the dose increased gradually according to tolerability.

Participants will attend visits for weight and body measurements, blood tests, side-effect assessments and questionnaires. Follow-up will continue for 26 weeks after the treatment period. Total follow-up from randomization will be 52 weeks for the immediate-start group and 78 weeks for the delayed-start group. Some participants will also be invited to interviews about their experience of treatment.
primary_outcomes: Completion of the 26-week semaglutide treatment phase meeting all composite feasibility criteria
title: Semaglutide for Weight Management During Hormone Therapy for Early Breast Cancer

brief_summary: This is a study to evaluate the efficacy of surovatamig combined with rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisone (R-CHOP) in participants aged 18 to \< 80 years of age with previously untreated large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL) with International Prognostic Index (IPI) score 2 to 5.
primary_outcomes: Progression free survival (PFS) as assessed by Blinded Independent Central Review (BICR)
title: A Study to Evaluate Surovatamig Combined With R-CHOP in Participants of 18 to < 80 Years of Age With Previously Untreated Large B-cell Lymphoma With IPI Score 2 to 5

brief_summary: Percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) is the preferred minimally invasive procedure for renal stones larger than 2 cm, staghorn calculi and complex stone burdens, but it is frequently associated with moderate-to-severe postoperative pain arising from the incision, renal capsular distension and visceral or stent-related sources. Truncal fascial plane blocks are a key component of opioid-sparing Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathways. The erector spinae plane block (ESPB) has accrued supportive evidence in PCNL, whereas the intertransverse process block (ITPB) - whose injectate target, the retro-superior costotransverse ligament space, lies closer to the paravertebral space than the ESPB target - has not been directly compared with ESPB in any urological surgery. This is a single-centre, prospective, stratified block-randomised, triple-blind, parallel-group superiority trial. A total of 140 patients undergoing elective unilateral PCNL under general anaesthesia will be randomised 1:1 to receive either ultrasound-guided ITPB or ESPB at the T10-T11 level before induction of anaesthesia, each with 20 mL of 0.375% ropivacaine (75 mg). Both groups will receive an identical intravenous patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) regimen (sufentanil 200 ug in 100 mL, 2 ug/mL; 1 mL bolus, 15-min lockout, no background infusion) for 48 h, with intravenous flurbiprofen axetil 50 mg as rescue. The primary outcome is cumulative opioid consumption over the first 48 postoperative hours, expressed as oral morphine equivalents (OME), calculated as OME (mg) = total sufentanil consumption (ug) x 3. The key secondary outcome is the area under the curve (AUC) of resting pain numeric rating scale (NRS) scores from 0 to 48 h. The hypothesis is that ITPB is superior to ESPB (that is, lower 48-h OME), with an expected between-group difference of -12 mg OME.
primary_outcomes: Cumulative opioid consumption within 48 hours after surgery, expressed as oral morphine equivalents (OME)
title: Intertransverse Process Block Versus Erector Spinae Plane Block for Postoperative Analgesia After Percutaneous Nephrolithotomy

brief_summary:
Wound dressing is a common procedure for children with injuries or wounds. The procedure can cause pain, fear, and anxiety. Children may also experience changes in heart rate and breathing when they feel distressed. Finding simple ways to help children cope with wound dressing may improve their experience of care.

This study examined changes in pain, anxiety, and physiological responses associated with playing interactive digital games during wound dressing. The study included 60 children aged 6-12 years who received wound dressing at the surgical department of Souad Kafafi University Hospital in 6th of October City, Egypt.

Each child selected an age-appropriate smartphone game and began playing approximately 1-2 minutes before wound dressing. The child continued playing throughout the procedure. Pain and anxiety were assessed, and physiological measurements, including pulse rate, breathing rate, and oxygen saturation, were recorded. The time required to complete wound dressing was also documented.

Measurements taken before and after the intervention were compared to examine changes associated with the use of digital games. The study aimed to determine whether interactive games could be a practical, child-friendly distraction to help children cope with pain and anxiety during wound dressing.

The findings may help nurses and other healthcare professionals consider the role of interactive digital games in pediatric wound care. Because the study used a single-group design without a separate control group, changes observed after the intervention cannot be attributed to the games alone.
primary_outcomes: Change in Anxiety Level Among Children Undergoing Wound Care
title: Healing Through Play

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if an internet-based Unified Protocol (iUP) intervention is effective for treating depression and anxiety disorders in Hong Kong young adults aged 18-29 years. This study is conducted within the eClinic, a public mental health support service provided by a Hong Kong non-government organisation (NGO). The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is the iUP intervention effective in treating depression and anxiety disorders?
* How long is the treatment effect sustained after the intervention ends?
* Does the intervention also improve real-world functioning, such as occupational and academic performance?

Researchers will compare participants who receive the iUP intervention immediately with those in a wait-list control group (who receive no intervention during the waiting period) to evaluate the effectiveness of iUP.

Participants will:

* Receive a 14-week iUP intervention either immediately or after a 14-week waiting period according to randomisation
* Complete weekly and follow-up questionnaires throughout the study period
primary_outcomes: Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9)
Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7)
title: Effectiveness of Internet-based Unified Protocol (iUP) for Emotional Problems: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, open, multi-cohort phase II study The study included a screening period (participants signed informed consent no more than 28 days before the first treatment in the study), a treatment period (treatment termination was defined as termination of treatment for any reason, such as imaging confirmation of disease progression, failure to tolerate adverse effects after dose adjustment, or early withdrawal for any reason), and a follow-up period (including end-of-treatment visits, safety visits, and survival follow-up).

Screening period: Participants are required to undergo a screening period within 28 days prior to the study's first treatment to determine eligibility.

Duration of treatment: Patients were treated with Cadonilimab in combination with lenvatinib until disease progression or intolerable toxicity developed. Every 3 weeks was a dosing cycle, and every 6 weeks was a treatment assessment.

Follow-up period: The safety follow-up period began after the last study treatment, and was followed up once on the 30th day (±7 days). Subjects should go to the research center for the examination of vital signs, physical examination, laboratory examination and other protocol requirements, and evaluate AE, concomitant medication and concomitant treatment.

After the end of the safety follow-up period, the subjects entered the 1-year survival follow-up period, which was conducted every 3 months. They could be visited by telephone follow-up and other effective ways to collect survival information and follow-up treatment information. Survival follow-up lasted until death, loss of follow-up, withdrawal

primary_outcomes: Objective Response Rate(ORR)

The study aims to explore the effect of group psychological intervention on academic distress among nursing undergraduates whose score on the self-developed Nursing Undergraduate Academic Distress Scale is ≥29. Eligible students will be randomly assigned to the intervention group or the control group. The intervention group will receive an 8-week structured group psychological intervention, while the control group will receive routine mental health education. The primary outcome is the change in academic distress score from baseline to the end of the 8-week intervention. Feasibility of the intervention program will also be evaluated.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if Justice Core, an intervention that moves pregnant women with substance use disorder (SUD) from jail into community-based SUD treatment while awaiting trial, can improve the health of pregnant women compared to referring them to treatment at the time of jail release. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Will the Justice Core intervention help women start and stay in SUD treatment compared to a group of women being given a treatment referral when they leave the jail?
* How does the Justice Core intervention affect pregnancy health outcomes compared with a group that is given a treatment referral when they leave the jail?
* What are the challenges in starting a new intervention, keeping it running, and the ethical issues during and after the trial?

Researchers will compare the outcomes of women who receive the Justice Core intervention with women who receive a treatment referral when they are released from jail. They will look at how many women start and continue treatment and compare pregnancy-related and incarceration outcomes.

Participants will be asked to:

* Complete a treatment assessment.
* Take part in three follow-up phone surveys.
* Some participants may also be asked to complete a longer phone interview to share more about their experiences.
lead_sponsor: University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill
primary_outcomes: Initiation of SUD treatment
Engagement in SUD treatment
title: Justice Core Trial

brief_summary: Postoperative differentiation between residual regional anesthetic effect and other causes of persistent sensory or motor deficit is a common clinical problem after peripheral nerve blocks. Perfusion index (PI), a noninvasive pulse oximetry-derived measure of peripheral perfusion, rises after sympathetic blockade and has been studied for predicting block success and duration. However, its ability to detect the resolution of a block has not been established. This prospective observational study will evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of the PI ratio between the blocked and contralateral hand for detecting sensory and motor block resolution in adult patients undergoing elective forearm surgery under ultrasound-guided infraclavicular brachial plexus block. PI, sensory block (pinprick), and motor block will be assessed repeatedly from before the block until 24 hours postoperatively. Cut-off values of the PI ratio for the first regression and the complete resolution of sensory and motor block will be determined using ROC analysis.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy of perfusion index ratio for resolution of motor block
Diagnostic accuracy of perfusion index ratio for resolution of sensory block
title: Perfusion Index in Monitoring Recovery From Brachial Plexus Block After Forearm Surgery

brief_summary: This retrospective observational study aims to evaluate the association between the lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR) measured at ICU admission and 28-day mortality in adult patients admitted to the intensive care unit with acute respiratory failure. interventions: Assessment of Admission Serum Lactate-to-Albumin Ratio (LAR)

brief_summary:
The goal of this Phase 1 clinical trial is to learn whether KAN-001, an investigational live biotherapeutic product, can be safely given with pembrolizumab, with or without chemotherapy, to adults with PD-L1-positive, inoperable or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* What side effects occur when KAN-001 is given with pembrolizumab, with or without chemotherapy?
* Can the microbial strains contained in KAN-001 be detected in participants' stool after treatment?

Participants will:

* Complete a bowel preparation before receiving the first dose of KAN-001.
* Take a loading dose of KAN-001, followed by maintenance doses every 3 weeks.
* Receive pembrolizumab every 3 weeks. Some participants will also receive chemotherapy.
* Provide blood, stool, and stool-wipe samples and complete a gastrointestinal symptom diary.
* Undergo imaging scans and other study assessments to monitor their cancer, health, and safety.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants With Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events
title: A Phase 1 Trial of KAN-001 With Pembrolizumab, With or Without Chemotherapy, in Participants With PD-L1-Positive Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer

brief_summary:
Brief Summary

The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if an accelerated, dual-protocol high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) intervention can treat and achieve long-term pain relief (analgesia) in patients with pharmacologically refractory primary Trigeminal Neuralgia (TN). The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can a combined 10 Hz and 20 Hz rTMS protocol significantly reduce average facial pain intensity (measured via the Visual Analog Scale) at 1 month post-treatment?
* Will the induced analgesic effect maintain clinical durability at the 3-month long-term longitudinal checkpoint?
* Can this non-invasive treatment significantly down-regulate secondary emotional distress (anxiety and depression) and improve the overall quality of life for chronic pain patients?

Participants will:

* Undergo a rigorous pre-screening process, including an outpatient clinical examination by an independent neurologist to confirm refractory TN, and a digital EEG to rule out epilepsy or other neurological counter-indications.
* Complete an initial baseline assessment using five standardized clinical tests (VAS, BPI, HADS, QoLp, and PGIC) to document pain intensity, symptom distribution, anxiety, depression, and baseline quality of life.
* Sign a formal Informed Consent form prior to starting any medical procedures.
* Receive non-invasive brain stimulation using the Neurosoft Neuro-MS/D magnetic stimulator, targeted at the primary motor cortex (M1) contralateral (opposite) to the painful facial side.
* Complete a 5-day compressed treatment course consisting of 10 total sessions delivered twice daily (a 28-minute 10 Hz protocol followed immediately by a 9-minute 20 Hz protocol per session) with a strict 45-50 minute rest interval between the two daily sessions, totaling 9,000 stimuli per day.
* Attend follow-up appointments exactly 1 month and 3 months after completing the treatment course to repeat the same clinical survey battery under identical conditions to track the durability of the therapeutic effect.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Patient-Reported Facial Pain Intensity via the Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
Long-Term Durability of Analgesia via the Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
title: Accelerated Dual-Protocol rTMS for Refractory Trigeminal Neuralgia

brief_summary: The goal of this observational study is to better understand how the amount of insulin people with type 1 diabetes are using relates to blood glucose control and the risk of complications. The main questions this study aims to answer are: 1) Is insulin dose related to the long-term risk of developing heart disease, kidney disease and other complications in people with type 1 diabetes, after accounting for blood glucose? and 2) Does insulin dose relate to early signs of heart and kidney disease (i.e., disease that is not clinically detectable) in people with type 1 diabetes who are using modern diabetes management regimens?

Time to First Instance of Severely Increased Albuminuria (SIA)
Time to Sustained Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) Decline

Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) Measurement
title: Relationship Between Insulin Dose and Complications in Type 1 Diabetes

brief_summary: Maternal milk is the gold standard in infant nutrition, providing significant advantages, in preterm and term infants. Maternal milk plays a major role in reducing the risk of inflammatory bowel disease(NEC) in premature and low birth weight infants as well as improving neurodevelopmental outcomes in this population, In this study the investigators are comparing earlier (from birth rather than 48 hours post delivery) use of an electrical breast pump. Mothers will be selected at random to be in one of two groups: early or later pump use. The investigators will compare milk volumes achieved on day 14 post delivery between the two groups. interventions: Hospital grade double electrical breast milk pump

brief_summary: The term "long COVID" refers to persistent, recurrent, or newly emerging symptoms following a biologically confirmed or suspected case of COVID-19 that are still present three months after the acute episode or positive test result, and that cannot be explained by a complication of the acute phase, a flare-up of a comorbid condition, or any cause other than COVID-19. The incidence of long Covid has primarily been estimated through the follow-up of cohorts of patients initially treated in the hospital, sometimes based on cohorts of patients who consulted a primary care physician, and rarely based on cohorts of individuals from an unselected source population who tested positive for Covid-19. Currently, there is little data available to estimate its overall burden in primary care and the general population (prevalence, incidence, healthcare utilization, symptom progression, and impact on quality of life). This study will consist of two arms: "general practice" and "general population." For each arm, an initial phase will involve simply counting cases, and a second phase will involve describing and monitoring cases over the course of one year, focusing on clinical outcomes, quality of life, and the patient care experience. The "general practice" arm will also include a study of the care experience from the perspective of general practitioners. Statistical analysis. For each arm of the study, the included patients will be described in terms of the various aspects under investigation: sociodemographic characteristics, history of COVID-19 infection, clinical presentation, quality of life, and psychological, professional, and family impact. The incidence and prevalence of cases seen in general practice will be estimated. Expected results and implications. The study will provide a better understanding of the disease and its impact, including for people who do not seek care for this reason. It will provide information to guide public policies regarding the care and treatment pathways for people suffering from long COVID.

title: Long Covid: Study of Quality of Life, Clinical Evolution and Use of Care. Cohort in General Practice and General Population in Metropolitan France COVILEV Study

brief_summary: Osteosarcopenia (OSP) is defined as the coexistence of sarcopenia and osteoporosis/osteopenia. There is an intense and complex interaction-both mechanical (the "mechanostat" hypothesis) and biochemical (involving factors such as estrogen, testosterone, GH, IGF-1, IL-6, and osteocalcin)-between osteoporosis and sarcopenia. The general consensus is that sarcopenia leads to a reduction in bone mineral density. OSP is associated with significant physical disability, which poses a major threat to the future loss of independence. The increased propensity for falls-a consequence of sarcopenia-compounds the risk of fractures associated with osteoporosis, further exacerbating adverse health outcomes. Kinesiophobia, or the "fear of movement," is an excessive and irrational dread of performing physical movements or activities, stemming from the fear of a painful injury or the possibility of re-injury; this often leads to restrictions in activities of daily living. In a clinical setting, kinesiophobia is a critical issue that must be addressed to effectively manage a patient's disability, as it directly influences rehabilitation strategies. While there is some limited literature exploring the individual associations of osteoporosis and sarcopenia with kinesiophobia, no research has yet examined the relationship between osteosarcopenia and kinesiophobia. Our study aims to determine the impact of osteosarcopenia on kinesiophobia and quality of life in postmenopausal women.
primary_outcomes: Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia
International Falls Efficacy Scale
Short Form-36 Health Survey (SF-36)
title: The Impact of Osteosarcopenia on Falls, Kinesiophobia, and Quality of Life in Postmenopausal Women

This completed randomized laboratory study investigated the immediate effects of a single 10-minute session of heart rate variability biofeedback (HRV-B) on cardiac activity, forehead physiological signals, and emotional responses in adults.

Heart rate variability reflects changes in the time intervals between heartbeats. HRV biofeedback provides real-time information about heart rhythm patterns and allows individuals to adjust their breathing in response to visual feedback.

Thirty-two adult participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups. Sixteen participants completed HRV biofeedback training using the emWave Pro Plus system, while 16 participants watched educational videos about biofeedback and breathing.

Heart rate variability was measured before, during, and after the intervention. Forehead physiological signals were recorded using hemoencephalography (HEG) before, during, and after the session. Positive and negative affect were assessed using questionnaires completed before and after the intervention.

The purpose was to compare immediate physiological and emotional responses between participants receiving active HRV biofeedback and those receiving psychoeducational information without real-time physiological feedback.

The original ethics-approved research proposal also included a planned non-invasive bioimpedance assessment of systemic inflammation. This component was not implemented, and no inflammation-related measurements were collected.
