brief_summary:
Gliomas are the most common and deadliest primary brain tumours in children and adults. Many people with glioma also develop epilepsy, which can be difficult to treat. Research suggests that inflammation in the brain and shared disease pathways may contribute to both glioma and epilepsy. Seizure-related electrical activity may also promote tumour growth and spread.

This study aims to investigate the relationship between blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction, glioma and epilepsy. The BBB normally protects the brain by regulating the movement of substances from the blood into brain tissue. Increased leakage across the BBB may indicate inflammation and may contribute to changes in brain structure and function.

Using a recently developed brain imaging technique, the study will measure BBB leakage in people with glioma, including those with and without tumour-related epilepsy, and in control participants without glioma or epilepsy. The researchers will compare imaging findings between these groups to investigate whether BBB leakage is associated with glioma and epilepsy, and whether it may be linked to structural changes in the brain.

The study will also examine whether the extent of BBB leakage is associated with tumour subtype and grade, and whether this imaging technique could help identify and characterise brain tumours. Finally, the researchers will compare the new imaging technique with conventional contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to assess its ability to detect subtle BBB leakage.

The findings may improve understanding of the relationship between BBB dysfunction, glioma and epilepsy, and help establish the potential value of advanced brain imaging in the diagnosis and assessment of gliomas.
primary_outcomes: Differences in inflammatory markers in people with glioma and healthy controls, as well as between people with glioma with and without epilepsy.
title: Blood Brain Barrier Dysfunction in Glioma and Epileptogenesis

brief_summary: Neurological diseases affect people's cognitive and physical abilities, limiting their functional independence and causing disability, which in many cases, is progressive and degenerative. Being able to perform activities of daily living is a challenge in these pathologies. Currently, different observational tools are administered to assess the degree of functional limitation in basic and instrumental Activities of Daily Living (ADL). However, the assessment must be performed in an ecological and real context to obtain objective information and ensure the most accurate assessment possible. To this end, it is necessary to consider the factors that influence the performance of ADLs and also on the quality of their execution, especially in this population in which the stressful situation of direct observation by an evaluator has a direct influence on the final score. NeurEYE aims to develop technological tools to extract from sensory systems typical of intelligent spaces and with the help of signal processing and machine learning processes based on artificial intelligence, indicators of neurological impairment that influence functional capacity and function/dysfunction components while observing the performance of an activity of daily living. In addition, NeurEYE would provide as a scientific breakthrough the accurate description of subjects' limitations in the controlled assessment environment within the routine patient context. The NeurEye project will allow the clinical validation of a multisensory system that, through the detection of functional limitations in the ADLs of patients with neurological disorder, allows to establish the level of disability of the subjects. In addition, the qualitative and quantitative description of the functional alterations of the person with neurological disorders and, the elimination of the subjective bias of the examiner, will allow the generation of individualized clinical and statistical reports according to sex, activity, etc. that will be clinically useful in the early detection, diagnosis, and adaptation of rehabilitation treatments to the specific functional needs of neurological disorders.

brief_summary:
Background Fluid management is central to perioperative care, but only about half of surgical patients increase their stroke volume after a fluid challenge. Dynamic indices such as pulse pressure variation and stroke volume variation are often unreliable during laparoscopy, because of low tidal volume ventilation and carbon dioxide (CO2) pneumoperitoneum. Functional hemodynamic tests may overcome these limitations. In the Mini fluid chAllenge aNd End-expiratory occlusion test to assess flUid responsiveness in the opeRating room (MANEUVER) study (NCT03808753), conducted in open abdominal surgery, the mini-fluid challenge predicted fluid responsiveness well, whereas the end-expiratory occlusion test did not. Pneumoperitoneum raises intra-abdominal pressure instead of abolishing it, so these results cannot be extrapolated to laparoscopy.

Design FLUID-LAP is a prospective, multicenter, observational diagnostic-accuracy cohort study conducted in four Italian centers and reported according to the Standards for Reporting of Diagnostic Accuracy (STARD) 2015 statement. Each patient is their own control: both index tests and the reference standard are performed in sequence in the same patient during a period of stable intraoperative hemodynamics, so the resulting receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves are correlated. The study replicates the design of MANEUVER, changing only the surgical setting. Ventilation (volume-controlled, 7 ml/kg predicted body weight), the reference fluid challenge and uncalibrated pulse-contour monitoring are the same, to allow direct comparison with the open-abdomen data.

Procedures Tests are performed under standardized baseline conditions (stable pneumoperitoneum and position, unchanged ventilation, no recent drug changes or surgical manipulation, arterial waveform checked with a square-wave test). The order of the two index tests is chosen by the attending anesthesiologist, is recorded for every patient, and is analyzed as a pre-specified covariate. A 3-minute return to steady state separates the tests. The complete 4 ml/kg fluid challenge is given after both tests. The maneuvers are already part of routine goal-directed practice, and no treatment decision is dictated by the protocol. Patient safety always prevails over the protocol.

Analysis The primary analysis compares the areas under the ROC curves (AUC) of the two tests using the DeLong test. The expected AUCs are 0.90 for the mini-fluid challenge and 0.75 for the end-expiratory occlusion test. With 80% power and a two-sided alpha of 0.05, 87 evaluable patients are required; 104 will be enrolled to allow for 15% attrition (26 per center). Pre-specified analyses address the mathematical coupling between the mini-fluid challenge and the reference challenge, the effect of test order, and subgroups by intra-abdominal pressure and patient position.
primary_outcomes: Difference in area under the ROC curve (AUC) between the mini-fluid challenge and the end-expiratory occlusion test for predicting fluid responsiveness
title: Fluid Responsiveness in Laparoscopic Surgery: End-Expiratory Occlusion Test Versus Mini-Fluid Challenge

Understanding the accuracy of fluoroscopic guidance of implants compared to transthoracic echocardiograms (TTE) and computed tomography angiography (CTA) of the heart will help guide future implant techniques. The implanter and two independent electrophysiologists will estimate the location of the implant based on standard fluoroscopic views using RV site nomenclature after the procedure. Each participant will then undergo a TTE and have 3 independent assessments of the implant site. Within 48 hours of the implant, a CTA of the heart will then be performed with contrast, which will serve as the gold standard to determine the actual implant site.

The primary endpoint will compare implanting electrophysiologist, fluoroscopy, and TTE predicted location of a new implanted Micra VR or AV2 leadless pacemaker to the implant location found on a gold standard CTA of the heart. The secondary endpoints will compare implant technique (Jugular vs. Femoral) by defining timing of implant procedure, repositioning, and accuracy of predicted implant location. The other secondary endpoints will compare baseline and demographic characteristics (BMI, COPD, LVEF, implant technique) to EKG parameters at final position, fluoroscopy and TTE image quality, acquisition of triangle or Koch and Bachmann area view during TTE.

brief_summary:
This study aims to improve how patients, families, and healthcare professionals work together to make important medical decisions, especially in cases involving hip fractures. Making treatment decisions after a hip fracture can be challenging, as it often involves weighing different options, risks, and expected outcomes. These decisions are particularly important for older adults, who may have other health conditions or personal priorities that influence their choices.

The study builds on previous research showing that Patient Decision Aids (PDAs) are valuable tools in supporting shared decision making (SDM). Shared decision making is a collaborative process in which healthcare providers and patients make decisions together, using both the best available medical evidence and the patient's personal values, preferences, and life circumstances. Rather than simply following a doctor's recommendation, patients are supported in understanding their options and actively participating in decisions about their care.

Patient Decision Aids are designed to make complex medical information easier to understand. They present clear, balanced, and structured information about available treatment options, including potential benefits, risks, and uncertainties. Many PDAs also use visual elements such as charts, diagrams, or icons to help users better grasp the information. Research has shown that these tools can improve patients' knowledge about their condition, increase their confidence in making decisions (known as decision self-efficacy), and lead to greater satisfaction with the decisions made. At the same time, PDAs can reduce decisional conflict, which refers to feelings of uncertainty, confusion, or stress when choosing between options. These benefits have been particularly evident in older populations and in decisions related to surgeries, such as joint replacement.

Despite these advantages, there is currently a lack of decision aids specifically designed for hip fracture-related decisions. Hip fractures are a common and serious health issue, especially among older adults, and they often require timely decisions about whether to undergo surgery, what type of surgery to choose, and how to manage recovery. This study seeks to address this gap by developing and evaluating a PDA tailored specifically for hip fracture treatment decisions.

The main objective of this study is to assess the usability of this newly developed decision aid. Usability refers to how easy the tool is to use, how clear and understandable the information is, and how helpful it is in supporting decision making. The PDA developed in this study combines clinical evidence with individual patient preferences and presents the information in a visual and user-friendly format. Its goal is to help patients, their families, and healthcare professionals make decisions that are consistent with what matters most to the patient.

Importantly, this study does not involve real medical treatment or interventions. Instead, it uses simulated scenarios in which participants are asked to imagine themselves or a loved one facing a hip fracture and needing to make treatment decisions. Because the study is based on simulation, there are no physical or medical risks involved.

The research is designed as an online randomized controlled trial with a parallel-group and pre-test/post-test structure. A total of 450 participants will be recruited. Eligible participants include individuals aged 20 and above who have experienced a hip fracture, have a family member who has experienced one, or belong to a group at higher risk of hip fractures.

Participation in the study is entirely voluntary. Participants have full freedom to decide whether to join and can withdraw from the study at any time without any consequences. Their participation or non-participation will not affect their medical care in any way.

At the beginning of the study, participants will complete a pre-test questionnaire to assess their baseline knowledge, confidence, and perceptions related to decision making. They will then be randomly assigned to one of two groups: an intervention group that uses the hip fracture decision aid, or a control group that does not use the tool. Participants will then take part in a simulated decision-making activity, which is expected to take about 30 to 60 minutes. After completing the scenario, they will fill out a post-test questionnaire.

All data collected during the study will be handled digitally and securely. Personal information will be removed so that participants cannot be identified, ensuring privacy and confidentiality. The researchers will analyze the data using appropriate statistical methods, depending on the type and distribution of the data collected. They will compare the two groups to evaluate differences in key outcomes, including knowledge about hip fracture treatment, confidence in decision making, level of decisional conflict, and satisfaction
conditions: High Risk Population of Hip Fractures
primary_outcomes: Knowledge of hip fracture surgery
Decision self-efficacy
Decisional conflict
Decisional satisfaction
title: A Decision Support Tool for Common Surgical Fixations of Hip Fractures

brief_summary: Background: Low-back pain is one of the most common health conditions worldwide. It is defined as pain below the costal margin and above the inferior gluteal folds. Due to aging, older adults experience pain, which can threaten their safety, autonomy, and independence, limit their social interactions, and reduce their quality of life. In exercise therapy, Pilates is considered effective for strengthening core muscles, improving muscle endurance, enhancing spinal control, and promoting trunk stability, thereby minimizing joint load. However, current research has focused on younger populations and lacks detailed descriptions of exercise interventions, making it unclear whether Pilates core exercises would benefit middle-aged and older adults.Therefore, this study incorporates resistance bands and yoga blocks into a Pilates regimen, emphasizing hip mobility exercises and gluteus medius strengthening to enhance the effectiveness of Pilates in treating chronic low back pain. This study aims to design a Pilates exercise therapy program for CLBP that includes hip mobility improvement and gluteus medius training to improve pain, disability level, hip mobility, gluteus medius strength, gluteal endurance, emotional function, participants' ratings of improvement and satisfaction, and participants' intention toward treatment.Purpose: This study targets individuals aged 40 to 69 with chronic low back pain and aims to:Develop an 8-week Pilates core exercise program focusing on gluteal strengthening and increased hip mobility, conducted three times per week for 60 minutes per session, to assess the effectiveness of primary outcome variables (pain, disability) and secondary outcome variables (emotional function, gluteus medius strength, gluteal endurance, hip mobility, satisfaction, self-efficacy).Methods: A single-blind randomized group design will be used in this study. Participants must be aged between 40 and 69 and have had low back pain for more than three months. They will be randomly assigned to either a control group or a Pilates intervention group.Outcome measurement:Outcome measurements include the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) for pain, the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), gluteus medius strength measured by microFET3, hip mobility, self-efficacy for exercise (SEE-C), and the Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC) scale.
lead_sponsor: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University
primary_outcomes: Pain was measured using a visual analogue scale (VAS).
Disability was assessed using the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI).
title: The Effectiveness of Pilates Exercise on Chronic Low Back Pain of The Older Adults

Severe crowding may have a negatively impact on oral health related quality of life particularly psychosocial well-being and self-perceived dental appearance.

In cases of severe crowding, extraction of four permanent teeth may be required to create sufficient space for proper alignment. Several treatment strategies are currently used, but there is a lack of scientific evidence regarding the optimal timing of tooth extraction and orthodontic treatment to achieve the best outcomes.

The trial compare 1) late first premolar extraction with fixed orthodontic treatment, (2) early first premolar extraction with planned fixed orthodontic treatment, and (3) early first premolar extraction followed by observation, with fixed treatment provided only if indicated. The study will evaluate treatment need, occlusal outcomes, spontaneous dental development, patient-reported outcomes, adverse effects, treatment efficiency, and cost-effectiveness.

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to evaluate the safety and impact of a protocolized respiratory physiotherapy program on the dynamics of systemic inflammatory biomarkers (procalcitonin \[PCT\] and C-reactive protein \[CRP\]) in critically ill adult patients with pneumonia in the intensive care unit (ICU), compared with standard medical care.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does a protocolized respiratory physiotherapy program accelerate the decline of PCT and CRP levels in critically ill patients with pneumonia compared to standard care? What is the incidence and safety profile of adverse events (e.g., transient desaturation, hemodynamic instability, or mechanical displacement) associated with respiratory physiotherapy sessions?

Researchers will compare a prospective cohort receiving structured respiratory physiotherapy against a historical control group receiving standard care to determine changes in inflammatory trajectories and ICU length of stay. Participants in the prospective intervention group will:

* Receive an individualized, protocolized respiratory physiotherapy regimen (including high-frequency chest wall oscillation \[HFCWO\], intrapulmonary acoustic percussion, positive expiratory pressure \[PEP\], and/or inspiratory muscle training \[IMT\]) tailored to their clinical deficits.
* Undergo continuous safety monitoring during and up to 30 minutes following each physiotherapy session.
* Have serum PCT and CRP levels measured at baseline (T0), Day 3 (T1), Day 7 (T2), and at ICU discharge (T3).
primary_outcomes: Adjusted Change in Procalcitonin (PCT) Levels
title: Respiratory Physiotherapy and Inflammatory Biomarkers in Critically Ill Patients With Pneumonia

* Have their blood pressure measured at clinic visits about every two weeks.
* Work with their kidney doctor on recommended changes to fluid management, peritoneal dialysis treatment, or blood pressure medicines to reach their assigned goal.
* Be part of the study for about four and a half months.
primary_outcomes: Feasibility of enrolling participants

These populations currently live with reduced functional ability due to reduced strength, motor control, and muscular endurance, thereby impairing their ability to perform tasks throughout the day. One of the common functional abilities lost is upper extremity (UE) function, which leads to decreased independence with activities of daily living (ADL), increased reliance on caregivers, and increased financial burden due to increased healthcare costs. Blood flow restriction therapy (BFR) is an innovative therapeutic intervention that may serve as a supplement to traditional interventions. Blood flow restriction therapy has shown promise in improving muscular hypertrophy, muscular strength, and functional outcome measures in those with and without neurologic conditions.

brief_summary:
Stroke is a major cause of long-term disability, and many stroke survivors experience persistent difficulties moving and using their affected arm and hand. Improving upper limb function is an important goal of stroke rehabilitation.

This study aims to investigate whether adding brain-machine interface (BMI) training to conventional rehabilitation improves upper limb motor recovery after stroke. The BMI system uses electroencephalography (EEG) to detect brain activity associated with imagined or attempted hand movements and provides visual feedback through virtual reality (VR). Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) is also applied to the affected wrist and finger extensor muscles during designated movement tasks.

A total of 68 adults undergoing inpatient rehabilitation after ischemic stroke will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups will receive standard rehabilitation. The experimental group will additionally receive BMI training with VR feedback and NMES, while the control group will receive NMES without BMI or VR feedback. Both groups will complete 12 additional sessions over four weeks.

The main outcome will be the change in upper limb motor impairment, assessed using the Fugl-Meyer Assessment for the Upper Extremity (FM-UE). Other measures will assess upper limb activity, muscle strength, and functional independence.

The study will help determine whether BMI-assisted training provides additional benefits compared with NMES alone when combined with conventional inpatient stroke rehabilitation.
interventions: Brain-Machine Interface Training With Virtual Reality and NMES
primary_outcomes: Change in Fugl-Meyer Assessment for the Upper Extremity (FM-UE) Score

The study consists of two phases. Phase 1 is a cross-sectional study to build and validate diagnostic models for COPD and asthma using IOS parameters, with respiratory specialists' clinical diagnosis as the gold standard. Phase 2 is a 48-week prospective cohort study to develop a prognostic model for predicting acute exacerbation risk based on IOS parameters. Approximately 2,800 participants will be enrolled from hospitals, physical examination centers, and community health centers across China. The results will provide evidence for the clinical application of IOS technology in chronic airway disease management.

brief_summary:
Spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) is a devastating form of stroke accounting for approximately 10-15% of all strokes globally. There is increasing evidence of younger working-age adults suffering from small-to-moderate sized spontaneous ICH, who develop significant motor and cognitive impairment after the event. These impairments contribute substantially to post-stroke functional morbidity and poor recovery, increasing care needs and decreasing economic productivity.

Existing neuromodulation trials in stroke rehabilitation have applied transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) at fixed anatomical targets using group-level brain maps, which overlooks the substantial inter-individual variability in the spatial topography of functional brain networks after ICH. Precision functional mapping techniques have demonstrated that individual-specific brain networks can be estimated using densely sampled resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) data and multi-session hierarchical Bayesian models (MS-HBM). These individual-specific networks can identify personalised neuromodulation targets for navigated TMS (nTMS) to improve rehabilitation outcomes.

Intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation (iTBS) to the primary motor cortex (M1) has been shown to alter functional connectivity in a dose-dependent manner, while iTBS to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) improves attention and memory after left-hemispheric stroke. Precision neuromodulation using nTMS targeting individual-specific functional M1 and DLPFC areas for personalised stroke rehabilitation has yet to be sufficiently tested in high-quality clinical trials.

The PREMANE trial aims to use precision functional mapping in individual patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage to investigate inter-individual connectivity changes over time and after navigated neuromodulation to deliver personalised neurorehabilitation for patients with ICH.
primary_outcomes: Fugl-Meyer Assessment: Upper Extremity
Montreal cognitive assessment score (MoCA)
Western Aphasia Battery
title: PREcision MApping and NEuromodulation After Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage: The PREMANE Trial

This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effects of a 12-week multidisciplinary intervention on muscle strength, postural alignment, and balance in older adults living in temporary container settlements following the February 2023 earthquakes in Kahramanmaraş, Türkiye.

A total of 60 adults aged 65 years and older were allocated to an intervention group (n=30) or a control group (n=30). The intervention group participated in an individualized health management program that included exercises targeting muscle strength, balance, mobility, and posture, together with nutritional counseling, psychosocial support, and health education. The control group received no active intervention and underwent assessments at baseline and after 12 weeks.

Muscle strength was assessed using digital and manual dynamometers. Postural alignment was evaluated using PostureScreen, while postural sway and balance were assessed using Gyko and functional performance tests, including the Timed Up and Go Test and Short Physical Performance Battery.

The study aimed to determine whether a multidisciplinary intervention could improve physical function, postural alignment, and balance in older adults living in post-disaster temporary housing.

Change in Postural Sway and Balance

brief_summary:
Repeated head impacts and concussions may be associated with cognitive difficulties and neurodegenerative changes in athletes. Although this association has been studied primarily in contact sports such as boxing and American football, professional football (soccer) players may also be exposed to repetitive head impacts through heading the ball and sustaining concussions.

This prospective study aims to evaluate the cognitive impact of repeated concussions in male and female outfield football players, including late-career and retired professional players. Cognitive function will be assessed using neuropsychological tests and questionnaires evaluating attention, concentration, executive functioning, subjective memory complaints, emotion regulation, anxiety, and depression. Multimodal brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) will also be performed to characterize brain imaging findings potentially associated with cumulative exposure to repetitive head impacts.

The findings may contribute to a better understanding of potential cognitive and neuroimaging abnormalities in football players and inform future long-term monitoring and preventive strategies.

brief_summary:
This multicenter, prospective observational study aims to learn whether a prediction model using routine clinical data, imaging findings (including spleen stiffness measurement), and circulating biomarkers can predict stent dysfunction and longer-term outcomes after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) in adults with portal hypertension. The main question it aims to answer is:

Does this model predict TIPS stent dysfunction within 1 year after the procedure, and does it perform better than Doppler ultrasound for assessing stent function? Secondary questions include whether the model can predict further decompensation, liver failure, recompensation, and liver-related death over 3 years, and whether periodontal status and circulating biomarkers are associated with adverse outcomes after TIPS.

About 1,490 participants aged 18-80 years who are scheduled to undergo TIPS as part of their routine medical care will be enrolled at multiple centers and followed for up to 3 years. This is an observational study; participants receive usual medical care, and no treatment is assigned by the study. No additional study-specific visits are required. Data will be collected from routine clinical records at baseline, during TIPS, within 1 week after TIPS, and at follow-up visits (1, 3, and 6 months, then every 6 months). Optional blood, stool, urine, gingival crevicular fluid, and subgingival plaque samples may be collected for biomarker and mechanism research. The primary endpoint is TIPS stent dysfunction within 1 year after the procedure.

primary_outcomes: TIPS stent dysfunction within 1 year after TIPS
title: Development and Validation of a TIPS Prognostic Model

brief_summary:
Background: Oral Lichen Planus (OLP) is a chronic, T-cell-mediated inflammatory disease of the oral mucosa, with the erosive form causing painful ulcerations and erosions, significantly impacting the patient's quality of life and carrying a risk of malignant transformation. While corticosteroids remain the first-line treatment, their long-term use is limited by significant local and systemic side effects. Consequently, there is a critical need for effective, non-invasive and safe alternative therapies. Photodynamic Therapy (PDT) and Photobiomodulation (PBM) have emerged as promising light-based modalities. Curcumin, a natural polyphenol, has gained attention as a safe and effective photosensitizer for PDT due to its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties.

Aim: This clinical trial aims to evaluate and compare the effect of nano-curcumin formulation incorporated into biodegradable mucoadhesive gel as a photosensitizer for Photodynamic Therapy (PDT) versus Photobiomodulation (PBM) in the treatment of oral erosive lichen planus.

brief_summary: This study evaluated whether a test formulation of sitagliptin/metformin tablets (manufactured by Jiangxi Shimei Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.) is bioequivalent to the reference product Janumet (sitagliptin phosphate/metformin hydrochloride tablets, MSD) in healthy Chinese adults. The study was conducted as two independent cohorts (fasting and fed) at a single centre. Each cohort used a randomised, open-label, two-period, two-sequence, single-dose crossover design with a 7-day washout between periods, and 28 subjects were enrolled in each cohort. In each period, subjects received a single oral dose of the test or the reference product, and serial blood samples were collected up to 48 hours after dosing to determine plasma sitagliptin and metformin concentrations with a validated analytical method. The primary pharmacokinetic parameters were Cmax, AUC0-t and AUC0-inf. Bioequivalence was to be concluded if the 90% confidence intervals of the geometric mean ratios (test/reference) for these parameters fell within the predefined acceptance range of 80.00%-125.00%. Currently, two main methods are used:Saline Bolus EIT: Involves injecting a saline solution during a breath-hold to track blood flow.Pulse Wave EIT: Utilizes cardiac-induced vascular pulsations to assess perfusion.However, both methods have limitations in ARDS patients, as the disease's altered physiology can affect their accuracy.

This study compares pulse wave versus saline bolus EIT for pulmonary perfusion assessment in ARDS patients and investigates the impact of different PEEP levels.

brief_summary:
The §SMOKE Cohort Study aims to improve understanding of tobacco and nicotine use among adolescents and young adults in Denmark. The study focuses on a rapidly changing nicotine landscape that includes cigarettes, e-cigarettes, nicotine pouches, heated tobacco products, and other nicotine products.

The study is based on the hypothesis that tobacco and nicotine use during adolescence and young adulthood follows different developmental pathways and that individual characteristics, social influences, and environmental factors affect initiation, continued use, cessation, relapse, and switching between products. The study further hypothesizes that different patterns of tobacco and nicotine use are associated with differences in educational, health, and social outcomes.

By following young people over time, the study seeks to improve understanding of how tobacco and nicotine use develops, which factors influence these behaviors, and what consequences may be associated with different patterns of use. The findings will contribute to evidence supporting tobacco and nicotine prevention efforts and public health policy for adolescents and young adults in Denmark.

brief_summary:
The study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of Multi Angular Isometric Lumbar Exercise (MAILE) in comparison to traditional lumbar stabilization and core stability treatments for managing nonspecific chronic low back pain (NCLBP). MAILE is designed to specifically target the Lumbo-Pelvic Hip complex with the goal of improving pain levels, stability, strength, and overall function.

Objectives of the study are to assess several key outcomes:

Pain Intensity: Measuring the level of pain experienced by patients. Functional Disability: Evaluating the impact of NCLBP on daily activities and overall function.

Functional Stability: Assessing the stability of the Lumbo-Pelvic Hip complex during movement.

Muscle Strength: Determining the strength of muscles within the targeted region.

By examining these outcomes, the research seeks to determine whether MAILE offers superior benefits and greater cost-efficiency compared to conventional treatments for patients with NCLBP and motor control dysfunction. If successful, MAILE could provide a more effective and economical approach to managing this common and debilitating condition. This Randomized Clinical Trial (RCT) will be conducted across multiple outpatient clinics within the Hamad Medical Corporation (HMC). The study will involve 98 patients diagnosed with non-specific chronic low back pain (NCLBP), who will be randomly assigned to one of two groups: the Multi Angular Isometric Lumbar Exercises (MAILE) group or the Core Stability group. Both groups will follow tailored exercise programs over a three-week period.

The MAILE group will focus on exercises designed to enhance lumbar stability and core strength through multi-angular isometric lumbar exercises performed at various angles. These exercises aim to target the deep stabilizing muscles of the lumbar spine, promoting overall spinal stability and reducing pain. The Core Stability group will engage in exercises that emphasize the activation and strengthening of the core muscles, which play a crucial role in maintaining spinal stability and function.

The outcomes of this trial will help determine the effectiveness of MAILE compared to traditional core stability exercises in managing NCLBP, potentially guiding future therapeutic strategies.
primary_outcomes: Visual Analogue Scale (VAS)
title: A Novel Treatment for Chronic Low Back Pain Using Multi Angular Isometric Lumbar Exercise: Randomized Clinical Trial.

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial will use a three-arm, parallel-group design to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 5-Hz Temporal Interference transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation (TI-tACS) in adults with generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). A total of 75 participants will be randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive stimulation targeting the right bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST), stimulation targeting the right amygdala, or sham stimulation. Participants will receive three 20-minute sessions per day, with 1-hour intervals between sessions, for 7 consecutive days (21 sessions in total). The primary outcome is the change in Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA) total score from baseline to Week 1. Secondary and exploratory assessments will include clinical symptoms, intolerance of uncertainty and related cognitive characteristics, treatment tolerability, adverse events, and EEG and MRI measures. brief_summary:
Background: Social media use is common among young people. However, uncontrolled use may become problematic and adversely affect psychological well-being and academic functioning, and cognitive behavioral approaches are a promising means of reducing problematic social media use.

Purpose: This study aimed to determine the effects of a cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT)-based psychoeducation programme (the Social Media Addiction Reduction Psychoeducation Programme- SMARPP) on problematic social media use and automatic thoughts in nursing students with mild-to-moderate problematic use. SMARPP was designed as an indicated preventive intervention, not as a treatment for clinically significant addiction.

Methods: In this randomized controlled study, 70 nursing students were allocated to an intervention (n = 35) or a no-intervention control (n = 35) group; 66 students (33 per group) completed all assessments. Data were collected using a general information form, Social Media Addiction Scale (SMAS), and Automatic Thoughts Questionnaire (ATQ). Group × time effects were analysed using linear mixed-effects models, and adjusted between-group differences were reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and Hedges' g; nonparametric analyses were retained as sensitivity analyses.
conditions: Problematic Social Media Use; Social Media Addiction; Negative Automatic Thoughts
primary_outcomes: Problematic social media use (Social Media Addiction Scale total score)
title: Effect of Cognitive Behavioral Approach Based Psychoeducation Program on Social Media Addiction and Automatic Thoughts in Nursing Students

brief_summary:
This study will examine whether virtual reality during planned cesarean birth reduces women's anxiety and improves their satisfaction with the birth experience.

The study will include 144 women undergoing elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia at Adana City Training and Research Hospital in Türkiye. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group will receive routine care and watch a relaxing nature video with natural sounds through a virtual reality headset during surgery. The other group will receive routine care alone.

Virtual reality will be paused when the baby is born so that anxiety can be assessed and the mother can see her baby. It will then resume until surgery ends.

Anxiety and vital signs will be assessed before surgery and 15-30 minutes after completion of surgery, once the participant is clinically stable. An additional brief anxiety assessment will be performed immediately after birth, before the mother first sees her baby. Satisfaction with cesarean birth will be assessed 6-8 hours after birth.

The researchers will compare the results between the two groups to evaluate the effects of virtual reality on maternal anxiety and cesarean birth satisfaction.
primary_outcomes: State Anxiety
title: Virtual Reality for Anxiety and Birth Satisfaction During Elective Cesarean Section

brief_summary:
This study aims to determine how many supervised practice attempts anesthesia trainees need to become competent in using ultrasound to assess the airway. Airway ultrasound may help clinicians identify anatomical features associated with a difficult airway, which can make breathing support or placement of a breathing tube more challenging during anesthesia. However, the amount of training needed to perform these ultrasound measurements accurately has not been established.

Eight anesthesia trainees will receive theoretical instruction and hands-on training before performing ultrasound assessments on 20 healthy adult volunteers. The trainees will measure tongue thickness and the distances from the skin to the epiglottis and vocal cords. Their measurements will be compared with those of experienced airway ultrasound experts to assess accuracy and determine how many attempts are needed to achieve competency. A follow-up assessment three months later will evaluate whether the trainees retain their skills.

The study hypothesis is that anesthesia trainees can achieve competency in airway ultrasound assessment after a limited number of supervised practice attempts and retain these skills over time. The findings may help establish evidence-based training requirements for airway ultrasound assessment.

brief_summary:
Long-standing unilateral facial paralysis is a complex functional and aesthetic disorder characterized by impaired facial movement, static asymmetry, and progressive soft-tissue changes. Chronic muscular imbalance and loss of tone may result in malar descent, distortion of the nasolabial fold, oral commissure malposition, jowling, reduced mandibular definition, and asymmetric facial aging. These deformities may persist despite successful dynamic facial reanimation.

Contemporary reanimation procedures, including masseteric-to-facial nerve transfer, cross-face nerve grafting, free functional muscle transfer, and temporalis transfer, can restore facial movement and improve dynamic symmetry. However, restoration of motor function does not necessarily correct residual static soft-tissue ptosis or asymmetry. Therefore, a staged approach addressing both dynamic function and static facial contour may be beneficial.

Deep-plane facelift techniques allow repositioning of the facial soft-tissue envelope through deep-plane mobilization and release of retaining ligaments. Their application in facial paralysis has recently been explored, but limited evidence exists regarding their use as a secondary procedure following established dynamic facial reanimation.

Comprehensive outcome assessment should incorporate clinician-reported, patient-reported, and objective measures. The eFACE and Facial Clinimetric Evaluation (FaCE) Scale provide complementary assessments of facial function and patient-perceived disability, while FACE-Q instruments can evaluate aesthetic and psychosocial outcomes.

Accordingly, this prospective study evaluates deep-plane facelift as a staged adjunct after stable facial reanimation, focusing on improvement in static facial symmetry and patient-perceived appearance while maintaining previously restored dynamic facial function.

This study was designed as a randomized controlled trial to determine the effect of positive psychology-based happiness workshops on the psychological resilience levels of nursing students. The study will be conducted between October 26, 2026, and January 26, 2026, with 102 fourth-year nursing students. Students who meet the inclusion criteria will be randomized and assigned to two groups: the experimental group (n=36) and the control group (n=36). All participating students will complete the "Demographic Information Form" and the "Psychological Resilience Scale for Nurses" (pre-test). Students in the experimental group will participate in happiness workshops for 4 weeks. All students in the control group will complete the "Demographic Information Form" and the "Psychological Resilience Scale for Nurses" (pre-test). No intervention will be administered to the students in the control group.

After the happiness workshops are completed, students in both the experimental and control groups will be administered the "Demographic Information Form" and the "Psychological Resilience Scale for Nurses" (post-test). Two months later, the "Demographic Characteristics Form" and the "Psychological Resilience Scale for Nurses" (follow-up test) will be administered to students in the experimental and control groups.

The collected data will be analyzed using SPSS 28 software.

This study aims to compare the effects of hip muscle strengthening with and without myofascial release of the calf muscle on pain and disability in females with chronic plantar fasciitis.

Chronic plantar fasciitis is a common cause of heel pain and may lead to limitations in walking, daily activities, and functional performance. Factors such as calf muscle tightness, restricted ankle dorsiflexion, altered lower-limb biomechanics, and proximal hip muscle weakness may contribute to persistent symptoms. Although strengthening exercises and myofascial release have shown beneficial effects, limited evidence is available regarding the combined effect of hip strengthening and calf myofascial release in females with chronic plantar fasciitis.

The study will be conducted as a randomized clinical trial with a total sample of 34 females, aged 25-45 years, who meet the specified criteria for chronic plantar fasciitis. Participants will be randomly allocated into two groups. Group A will receive hip muscle strengthening exercises, while Group B will receive the same strengthening program combined with myofascial release of the calf muscles. Both groups will receive treatment three times per week for six weeks, for a total of 18 sessions.

The primary outcome measures will include the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS), Foot Function Index (FFI), and Morning First-Step Pain Visual Analogue Scale (VAS). Assessments will be performed at baseline and after completion of the six-week intervention.

In this trial, researchers want to learn if giving sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) alone or with other treatments can treat mCRPC. * How many participants have the cancer respond (gets smaller or goes away) to the trial treatments
* About the safety of the trial treatments and if participants tolerate the treatments. Tolerate means participants will receive the trial treatments unless they need to stop it due to health problems.

brief_summary:
The Vendor Business School for Healthy Diets (VBS-4HD) study is a research project designed to examine whether supporting small-scale fruit and vegetable vendors with knowledge on food handling and business management, as well as marketing skills, can contribute to healthier diets in urban communities.

The Philippines is facing growing nutrition challenges. Rates of overweight, obesity, and diet-related non-communicable diseases have increased steadily over the past decade, particularly in urban areas. At the same time, many Filipinos continue to experience food insecurity, and consumption of fruits and vegetables remains below recommended levels. Despite national and local efforts to promote healthy eating, many people still consume diets high in sugary, salty, and fatty foods and low in fresh produce.

Research suggests that unhealthy diets are influenced by several factors, including busy urban lifestyles, the increasing availability and promotion of convenience foods, limited awareness of healthy dietary recommendations, cultural food preferences, and weaknesses in food systems that make healthy foods less visible or attractive than processed alternatives. New approaches are needed to encourage healthier food choices in everyday settings.

In Philippine cities, local markets, street vendors, and small food kiosks remain the main source of fresh foods for many households. These informal food outlets play a critical role in urban food systems and provide livelihoods for large numbers of people, particularly women. Recognizing their importance, the Quezon City Government, in partnership with CGIAR researchers, established the Vendor Business School (VBS) in 2024. The program provides market vendors with training and individualized coaching in business management, food safety, and customer relations. Early implementation showed high levels of vendor satisfaction and positive business outcomes, leading to the institutionalization of the program through a city ordinance.

Building on this experience, the VBS-4HD research study explores whether market vendors can also become effective promoters of healthy diets. The study is based on the idea that vendors interact with customers every day and may therefore be uniquely positioned to encourage healthier food choices.

The VBS4HD study will evaluate a package of activities consisting of training, coaching, and marketing support delivered to small-scale fruit and vegetable vendors operating in private urban markets in Quezon City. The program aims to strengthen vendors' food hygiene and handling practices, improve their business performance, and encourage them to actively promote fruit and vegetable consumption among their customers.

The research will compare outcomes in markets where vendors receive the VBS-4HD program with outcomes in markets operating as usual. The study will assess whether the program leads to improvements in vendors' food handling practices and monthly profits, and whether it increases fruit and vegetable consumption among women aged 20-49 years living in customer households that regularly purchase produce from participating vendors.

The findings will contribute to understanding whether informal market vendors can serve as effective partners in improving urban diets and nutrition. The study will generate evidence to inform local governments, policymakers, and development organizations seeking practical and scalable approaches to promote healthier food environments, strengthen local food systems, and support healthier communities.

brief_summary:
Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic condition characterized by high blood glucose levels due to insufficient insulin production or the body's inability to respond properly to insulin. One of its common complications is diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN), which develops when prolonged high blood glucose levels damage peripheral nerves, particularly those in the lower limbs and feet. Patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathy may experience burning pain, tingling, numbness, muscle weakness, and loss of sensation. The condition can also affect balance and walking ability, making daily activities difficult. Reduced sensation increases the risk of unnoticed injuries, foot infections, ulcers, and other serious complications.

A randomized controlled trial was conducted involving 38 participants, divided into two groups. Group A received tibial nerve mobilization along with conventional physiotherapy, while Group B received multisensory exercise training along with conventional physiotherapy. According to the abstract, both interventions were delivered for 35 minutes per session, three sessions per week, over four weeks.

The aim of this study is to determine the comparison of multisensory exercise and tibial nerve mobilization in patients with type 2 diabetic peripheral neuropathy.

This retrospective observational cohort study evaluated whether rectal administration of mother's own milk was associated with feeding progression and growth in preterm infants. The study included 50 infants born between 27+0 and 32+6 weeks of gestation at a neonatal intensive care unit in Baku, Azerbaijan, between January 2023 and January 2026. All infants had delayed meconium passage beyond 48 hours after birth.

Of the 50 infants, 29 received rectal administration of mother's own milk as part of clinical care, while 21 did not receive this intervention. Treatment was not randomly assigned. The primary outcome was time to full enteral feeding. Secondary outcomes included time to full oral feeding, hospital stay, and weight, length, and head circumference at 36 and 40 weeks' postmenstrual age.

The study aimed to explore whether this clinical practice was associated with improved feeding and growth outcomes and to provide preliminary evidence for future clinical trials.
interventions: Rectal Administration of Mother's Own Milk

Each patch is used for at least 14 days, for 8 hours per day, with a washout of at least 14 days between periods. Participants and researchers know which patch is used. Wearable measurements are compared within the same participant across the two patch periods. Questionnaires are completed at the beginning and end of each period.

brief_summary:
This study is a single-center, prospective clinical study that plans to prospectively recruit volunteers aged 18-40 years, including metabolically healthy individuals and those with diabetes mellitus and hyperlipidemia. brief_summary: This study is a retrospective real-world study based on the electronic medical record database of Nanjing First Hospital. By integrating data from the hospital information system, ultrasound system, endoscopy system, pathology system, surgery and anesthesia system, medical record front pages, laboratory system, and electronic medical records, the study aims to evaluate the relationship between a history of cholecystectomy and biliary tract-related diseases and the detection risk of colorectal adenoma, and further analyze their associations with advanced lesions including advanced adenoma, high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia, adenoma carcinogenesis, or colorectal cancer. Additionally, it will explore the impact of different biliary disease subtypes, time intervals after cholecystectomy, and adenoma location on the study results. If the study finds that cholecystectomy or specific biliary diseases are associated with an increased risk of colorectal adenoma and advanced lesions, it may provide a reference for risk stratification of colorectal tumor screening and optimization of colonoscopy follow-up strategies for patients with biliary diseases; if no clear association is found, it may also provide evidence for clinically reasonable assessment of screening needs and avoidance of over-examination.

brief_summary: Children with sepsis, a condition in which infection causes organ dysfunction will be enrolled with parental permission in this study. The investigators will measure whether normalization of metabolism with this personalized nutrition leads to resolution of organ dysfunction.
